title.zh: 卷60 韓麒麟 程駿
title.raw: 卷60 韓麒麟 程駿 Volume 60: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun

sentences.zh: 韓麒麟 程駿

translations.literal: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun
translations.idiomatic: Han Qilin and Cheng Jun

sentences.zh: 後參征南慕容白曜軍事，進攻升城，師人多傷。

translations.literal: Later he joined the military affairs of the Campaign South general Murong Baiyao, attacked Shengcheng, and many in the army were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the staff of Murong Baiyao, the Campaign South general, in the assault on Shengcheng, where the army suffered heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，白曜將坑之，麒麟諫曰：「今始踐偽境，方圖進取，宜寬威厚惠，以示賊人，此韓信降范陽之計。

translations.literal: When the city collapsed, Baiyao was about to bury them alive. Qilin remonstrated, saying: "We have only now trodden the territory of the usurpers and are planning to advance further. We should temper severity with generous favor to show the enemy—this is Han Xin's stratagem for reducing Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Baiyao prepared to massacre the captives by burying them alive. Qilin urged him: "We have only just entered the usurpers' territory and are still planning our advance. We ought to temper severity with generous clemency as a signal to the enemy—this is the same strategy Han Xin used to win over Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 勁敵在前，而便坑其眾，恐自此以東，將人各為守，攻之難克。

translations.literal: With strong enemies ahead, yet at once burying alive the masses—I fear that from here eastward commanders will each hold their own defenses, and attacks will be hard to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: With formidable enemies still ahead, to slaughter the populace now would likely drive every commander east of here to hold his ground independently, making the region far harder to conquer.

sentences.zh: 日久師老，外民乘之，以生變故，則三齊未易圖也。」

translations.literal: As days lengthen the army grows weary; outsiders will seize the opportunity to stir up incidents—then the three Qi will not be easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: As the campaign drags on the army will tire, outsiders will seize their chance to stir up trouble, and the three Qi regions will no longer be easy to bring under control."

sentences.zh: 白曜從之，皆令復業，齊人大悅。

translations.literal: Baiyao followed this, had them all return to their occupations, and the people of Qi were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao accepted his advice, restored everyone to their livelihoods, and the people of Qi were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 後白曜表麒麟為冠軍將軍，與房法壽對為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Baiyao memorialized Qilin as Champion General, paired with Fang Fashou as Jizhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao later recommended Qilin for appointment as Champion General, to serve jointly with Fang Fashou as inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 白曜攻東陽，麒麟上義租六十萬斛，并攻戰器械，於是軍資無乏。

translations.literal: When Baiyao attacked Dongyang, Qilin presented righteous tribute of six hundred thousand hu of grain, together with siege weapons—thus military supplies were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: During Baiyao's siege of Dongyang, Qilin supplied six hundred thousand hu of grain as voluntary tribute, along with siege equipment, so that the army never wanted for provisions.

sentences.zh: 及白曜被誅，麒麟亦徵還，停滯多年。

translations.literal: When Baiyao was executed, Qilin was also summoned back and remained idle for many years.
translations.idiomatic: After Baiyao was put to death, Qilin too was recalled to court and languished without appointment for many years.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，拜給事黃門侍郎，乘傳招慰徐兗，叛民歸順者四千餘家。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Gaozu he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, rode post-horses to console Xu and Yan, and over four thousand households of rebel populace submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent by post-chaise to pacify Xu and Yan; more than four thousand rebel households came back into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 尋除冠軍將軍、齊州刺史，假魏昌侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Champion General and Qizhou inspector, with provisional title Marquis of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Champion General and inspector of Qizhou, with the provisional title Marquis of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 麒麟在官，寡於刑罰，從事劉普慶說麒麟曰：「明公仗節方夏，而無所斬戮，何以示威？」

translations.literal: While Qilin held office he was sparing in punishments. His aide Liu Puqing urged Qilin, saying: "My lord, you bear credentials in the height of summer yet have made no executions—how will you display authority?"
translations.idiomatic: In office Qilin was sparing with punishments. His aide Liu Puqing pressed him: "My lord, you hold imperial commission in the height of summer yet have not ordered a single execution—how can you inspire awe?"

sentences.zh: 麒麟曰：「刑罰所以止惡，蓋不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Qilin said: "Punishments exist to stop evil—they are used only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin replied: "Punishment exists to restrain wickedness and should be used only when there is no other choice.

sentences.zh: 今民不犯法，何所戮乎？

translations.literal: Now the people commit no offenses—whom should I punish?
translations.idiomatic: The people are not breaking the law—whom am I to execute?

sentences.zh: 若必須斬斷以立威名，當以卿應之。」

translations.literal: If executions are truly required to establish a reputation for authority, you yourself should answer for it."
translations.idiomatic: If heads truly must fall to establish my reputation, then you yourself should supply the example."

sentences.zh: 普慶慚懼而退。

translations.literal: Puqing withdrew in shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Puqing withdrew, ashamed and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 麒麟以新附之人，未階臺宦，士人沉抑，乃表曰：「齊土自屬偽方，歷載久遠，舊州府僚，動有數百。

translations.literal: Qilin, considering that newly submitted people had not entered court offices and scholars were suppressed, submitted a memorial saying: "Qi territory has long belonged to the usurping regime; former prefectural staff number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Because men newly brought under the dynasty had not yet risen to court posts and local scholars remained sidelined, Qilin submitted a memorial: "Qi has long been under the southern regime; former prefectural staffs alone run to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 自皇威開被，并職從省，守宰闕任，不聽土人監督。

translations.literal: Since imperial authority spread, offices were merged and reduced; when prefects and magistrates were vacant, locals were not allowed to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's authority reached this land, offices were merged and trimmed; when prefects and magistrates were unfilled, local men were not permitted even to oversee affairs.

sentences.zh: 竊惟新人未階朝宦，州郡局任甚少，沉塞者多，願言冠冕，輕為去就。

translations.literal: I reflect that newcomers have not risen to court posts; few appointments exist in prefectures and commanderies; many are blocked—those who seek caps and robes lightly come and go.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that newcomers still hold no court rank, that few posts remain open in the provinces, and that many capable men are shut out; those who seek official caps and robes therefore come and go with little loyalty.

sentences.zh: 愚謂守宰有闕，宜推用豪望，增置吏員，廣延賢哲。

translations.literal: I humbly propose that when prefects and magistrates are vacant, local magnates should be promoted, offices increased, and worthy men widely recruited.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest that when prefects and magistrates are lacking, local leaders of standing should be promoted, the number of posts increased, and worthy men sought far and wide.

sentences.zh: 則華族蒙榮，良才獲敍，懷德安土，庶或在茲。」

translations.literal: Then eminent families would receive honor, able men gain employment, and cherishing virtue while settling on the land—perhaps this lies therein."
translations.idiomatic: Then eminent clans would share in honor, able men would find employment, and gratitude for imperial grace together with attachment to the land might be secured by this means."

sentences.zh: 朝議從之。

translations.literal: The court deliberation accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 太和十一年，京都大饑，麒麟表陳時務曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe the capital suffered great famine; Qilin memorialized on current affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Taihe era a great famine struck the capital; Qilin submitted a memorial on urgent policy matters, stating:

sentences.zh: 古先哲王經國立治，積儲九稔，謂之太平。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings in governing the state and establishing order stored grain for nine years and called this peace.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity, in ordering the state and establishing rule, laid up grain for nine harvests and called that true peace.

sentences.zh: 故躬籍千畝，以勵百姓，用能衣食滋茂，禮教興行。

translations.literal: Therefore they personally plowed the thousand-mu field to encourage the people, and thus clothing and food flourished and ritual teaching arose.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore plowed the sacred field themselves to encourage the people, so that food and clothing abounded and ritual and instruction flourished.

sentences.zh: 逮於中代，亦崇斯業，入粟者與斬敵同爵，力田者與孝悌均賞，實百王之常軌，為治之所先。

translations.literal: Down to the middle ages this pursuit was also honored: those who contributed grain received the same rank as those who beheaded enemies; those who labored in the fields received rewards equal to the filial and fraternal—truly the constant track of the hundred kings and the first priority of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Even in later ages rulers prized the same work: men who contributed grain were ennobled like men who slew enemies in battle, and diligent farmers were rewarded like men famed for filial piety—this has been the constant practice of the hundred kings and the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 今京師民庶，不田者多，遊食之口，三分居二。

translations.literal: Now among the populace of the capital many do not farm; of mouths that wander and consume, two parts in three.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the capital many common people do not till the soil; idlers and dependents make up two thirds of the population.

sentences.zh: 蓋一夫不耕，或受其飢，況於今者，動以萬計。

translations.literal: For if one man does not plow, others may suffer hunger—how much more today, when they number in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When one man fails to farm, others may go hungry; how much worse when the idle number in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 故頃年山東遭水，而民有餒終；

translations.literal: Thus in recent years when Shandong suffered floods, some among the people starved to death;
translations.idiomatic: That is why, when floods struck Shandong in recent years, people there actually starved to death;

sentences.zh: 今秋京都遇旱，穀價踊貴。

translations.literal: this autumn the capital met drought and grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: and this autumn drought in the capital has sent grain prices soaring.

sentences.zh: 實由農人不勸，素無儲積故也。

translations.literal: This truly stems from farmers not being encouraged and from having no stored reserves.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is that farming has not been encouraged and no reserves have been built up.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天縱欽明，道高三、五，昧旦憂勤，思恤民弊，雖帝虞一日萬幾，周文昃不暇食，蔑以為喻。

translations.literal: I bow and reflect that Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with reverent brilliance, your Way surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, rising before dawn in anxious diligence to think of relieving the people's ills—though Emperor Shun handled ten thousand affairs in a day and King Wen at sunset had no leisure to eat, these are not fit comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with sagely brilliance; your Way surpasses even the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors; you rise before dawn in anxious toil to ease the people's hardships—yet even Emperor Shun's ten thousand affairs a day and King Wen's meals taken only at sunset scarcely suffice as comparisons.

sentences.zh: 上垂覆載之澤，下有凍餒之人，皆由有司不為明制，長吏不恤其本。

translations.literal: Above there spreads the grace that covers and carries all; below are people frozen and starving—all because the offices do not set clear regulations and chief officials do not care for fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while imperial grace covers all like heaven and earth, below there are people who freeze and starve—because the ministries have not framed clear laws and local chiefs have neglected the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 自承平日久，豐穰積年，競相矜夸，遂成侈俗。

translations.literal: Since peace has lasted long and harvests have been abundant for years, people vie in boasting until an extravagant custom has formed.
translations.idiomatic: Peace has lasted so long and harvests have been rich for so many years that people compete in display until extravagance has become custom.

sentences.zh: 車服第宅，奢僭無限；

translations.literal: Carriages, dress, mansions, and estates—extravagance and presumption without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Carriages, clothing, mansions, and estates know no limit of luxury or presumption;

sentences.zh: 喪葬婚娶，為費實多；

translations.literal: funerals, weddings, and marriages cost truly much;
translations.idiomatic: funerals, weddings, and betrothals consume vast sums;

sentences.zh: 貴富之家，童妾袨服；

translations.literal: in wealthy and noble houses, child concubines wear splendid dress;
translations.idiomatic: in rich and noble households even child concubines dress in finery;

sentences.zh: 工商之族，玉食錦衣。

translations.literal: merchant and artisan clans eat jade-like food and wear brocade.
translations.idiomatic: merchant and artisan families feast on delicacies and clothe themselves in brocade.

sentences.zh: 農夫餔糟糠，蠶婦乏短褐。

translations.literal: Farmers eat chaff and bran; silkwomen lack short hemp garments.
translations.idiomatic: While farmers eat chaff and bran, women who tend silkworms lack even coarse hemp to wear.

sentences.zh: 故令耕者日少，田有荒蕪。

translations.literal: Thus tillers grow fewer day by day and fields lie waste.
translations.idiomatic: Hence tillers grow fewer by the day and fields fall idle.

sentences.zh: 穀帛罄於府庫，寶貨盈於市里；

translations.literal: Grain and cloth are exhausted in the treasuries while treasures overflow in the markets;
translations.idiomatic: Grain and cloth are drained from the treasuries while valuables pile up in the markets;

sentences.zh: 衣食匱於室，麗服溢於路。

translations.literal: food and clothing are scarce in homes while gorgeous dress spills into the roads.
translations.idiomatic: yet food and clothing are scarce within homes while gorgeous dress spills into the streets.

sentences.zh: 飢寒之本，實在於斯。

translations.literal: The root of hunger and cold lies truly here.
translations.idiomatic: The root of hunger and cold lies here.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡珍玩之物，皆宜禁斷，吉凶之禮，備為格式，令貴賤有別，民歸朴素。

translations.literal: I humbly propose that all precious curios should be forbidden, that auspicious and inauspicious rites be fully set in format, so that noble and humble are distinguished and the people return to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly propose that precious luxuries be banned outright, that rites for weddings and funerals be codified in full, and that distinctions of rank be enforced so the people may return to simplicity.

sentences.zh: 制天下男女，計口受田。

translations.literal: Regulate males and females throughout the realm to receive fields by head count.
translations.idiomatic: Assign fields throughout the realm to men and women according to household size.

sentences.zh: 宰司四時巡行，臺使歲一按檢。

translations.literal: Chief officials should tour in the four seasons; imperial commissioners should inspect once a year.
translations.idiomatic: Let chief officials tour the fields in all four seasons and imperial commissioners conduct an annual inspection.

sentences.zh: 勤相勸課，嚴加賞賜。

translations.literal: Diligently encourage and supervise farming; strictly add rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Encourage farming diligently and reward it generously.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，必有盈贍，雖遇災凶，免於流亡矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years there will surely be surplus; even if disaster strikes, people will be spared from wandering in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years there will surely be surplus grain; even if disaster strikes, the people will be spared mass flight.

sentences.zh: 往年校比戶貫，租賦輕少。

translations.literal: In recent years when household registers were checked and compared, rents and levies were light and few.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, when household registers were checked and compared, rents and levies were set low.

sentences.zh: 臣所統齊州，租粟纔可給俸，略無入倉。

translations.literal: In Qizhou, which I administer, grain rent barely suffices for salaries and scarcely enters the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Qizhou, which I administer, grain rents barely cover official salaries and almost nothing reaches the public granaries.

sentences.zh: 雖於民為利，而不可長久。

translations.literal: Though this benefits the people, it cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: That may benefit the people in the short term, but it cannot be sustained.

sentences.zh: 脫有戎役，或遭天災，恐供給之方，無所取濟。

translations.literal: If there should be military campaigns or heaven-sent disasters, I fear there will be no source from which to draw supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Should war break out or heaven send disaster, I fear there will be no reserve from which to draw relief.

sentences.zh: 可減絹布，增益穀租，年豐多積，歲儉出賑。

translations.literal: Silk and cloth levies could be reduced and grain rents increased; in abundant years store more, in lean years distribute relief.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and cloth levies could be reduced while grain rents are increased; store more in good years and release grain for relief in lean ones.

sentences.zh: 所謂私民之穀，寄積於官，官有宿積，則民無荒年矣。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by the people's private grain deposited in accumulation with the state—when the state has stored reserves, the people will have no famine years.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by the people's grain held in trust by the state: when the government keeps reserves, the people need not face famine.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，卒於官，年五十六。

translations.literal: In spring of the twelfth year he died in office, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twelfth year he died in office at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 遺敕其子，殯以素棺，事從儉約。

translations.literal: He left instructions to his sons to bury him in a plain coffin and keep the rites frugal.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to his sons to bury him in an unadorned coffin and keep the funeral simple.

sentences.zh: 麒麟立性恭慎，恒置律令於坐旁。

translations.literal: Qilin's nature was respectful and cautious; he always kept the statutes at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin was by nature respectful and cautious and always kept the law codes at his side.

sentences.zh: 臨終之日，唯有俸絹數十匹，其清貧如此。

translations.literal: On the day of his death he had only several dozen bolts of salary silk—such was his integrity and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he possessed only a few dozen bolts of his official salary silk—such was his integrity and poverty.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安東將軍、燕郡公，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Pacification-East General, and Duke of Yan Commandery, with posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Pacification-East General, and Duke of Yan Commandery, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子興宗，字茂先。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingzong, style Maoxian.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Xingzong, whose style was Maoxian.

sentences.zh: 好學，有文才。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 年十五，受道太學。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he received the Way at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 後司空高允奏為祕書郎，參著作事。

translations.literal: Later the Minister of Works Gao Yun memorialized him as Secretariat Gentleman to participate in compilation work.
translations.idiomatic: Later Minister of Works Gao Yun recommended him as Secretariat Gentleman to take part in the historiographical office.

sentences.zh: 中山王叡貴寵當世。

translations.literal: Prince Rui of Zhongshan was honored and favored in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Zhongshan enjoyed extraordinary favor in his day.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna in the text.〉

sentences.zh: 為文。

translations.literal: composed writings.
translations.idiomatic: He composed literary pieces for the prince.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書中散。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太和十四年冬，卒。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourteenth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the fourteenth year of the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 贈寧遠將軍、漁陽太守。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Pacification-Distant General and Administrator of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Pacification-Distant General and administrator of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 子子熙，字元雍。

translations.literal: His son Zixi, style Yuanyong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zixi, whose style was Yuanyong.

sentences.zh: 少自修整，頗有學識。

translations.literal: From youth he cultivated himself and had considerable learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he cultivated himself carefully and possessed considerable learning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，未能自通，侍中崔光舉子熙為清河王懌常侍，遷郎中令。

translations.literal: At weak-crown he had not yet made his own way; Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang recommended Zixi as Regular Attendant to Prince Yi of Qinghe, and he was promoted to Chief of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Coming of age, he had not yet found a post on his own; Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang recommended Zixi as regular attendant to Prince Yi of Qinghe, after which he rose to chief of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，子熙父以爵讓弟顯宗，不受。

translations.literal: At first Zixi's father yielded his noble rank to his younger brother Xianzong, who did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zixi's father had tried to yield his noble title to his younger brother Xianzong, who refused it.

sentences.zh: 子熙緣父素懷，卒亦不襲。

translations.literal: Zixi, following his father's longstanding intent, in the end also did not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring his father's longstanding wish, Zixi in the end did not inherit the title either.

sentences.zh: 及顯宗卒，子熙別蒙賜爵，乃以其先爵讓弟仲穆。

translations.literal: When Xianzong died, Zixi separately received a bestowed noble rank and then yielded his earlier rank to his younger brother Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong died, Zixi received a separate ennoblement and then yielded his original title to his younger brother Zhongmu.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was the brothers' mutual affection.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the brothers' mutual devotion.

sentences.zh: 父亡，居喪有禮。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 子熙為懌所眷遇，遂闕位，待其畢喪後復用。

translations.literal: Zixi was favored by Yi, who therefore left the post vacant and waited to employ him again after mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prince favored Zixi, he left the post vacant until mourning was finished and then took him back into service.

sentences.zh: 及元叉害懌，久不得葬。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha harmed Yi, burial was long impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha brought about Prince Yi's death, proper burial was long delayed.

sentences.zh: 子熙為之憂悴，屏處田野，每言王若不得復封，以禮遷葬，誓以終身不仕。

translations.literal: Zixi grieved and wasted away over this, withdrew to the countryside, and often said that if the Prince were not restored to his fief and properly reburied, he swore never to take office for life.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was consumed with grief, withdrew to live in the countryside, and declared that unless the prince were restored to his fief and given a proper burial he would never take office again as long as he lived.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后返政，以元叉為尚書令，解其領軍。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling returned to power, made Yuan Cha Minister of the Masters of Writing, and removed him from command of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Empress Dowager Ling resumed power, Yuan Cha was made Minister of the Masters of Writing and stripped of his command over the guards.

sentences.zh: 子熙與懌中大夫劉定興、學官令傅靈𢷋、賓客張子慎伏闕上書曰：

translations.literal: Zixi, together with Yi's Grand Master of the Palace Liu Dingxing, Director of Studies Fu Lingxie, and Retainer Zhang Zishen, lay prostrate at the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zixi, together with Prince Yi's palace grandee Liu Dingxing, director of studies Fu Lingxie, and retainer Zhang Zishen, prostrated themselves at the palace gate and submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 竊惟故主太傅清河王，職綜樞衡，位居論道，盡忠貞以奉公，竭心膂以事國，自先皇崩殂，陛下沖幼，負扆當朝，義同分陝。

translations.literal: I humbly reflect on our late lord the Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe: his office embraced the pivot of state, his position was to discourse on the Way; he exhausted loyalty and constancy in serving the public good and poured out heart and sinew in serving the state. Since the late emperor's demise, when Your Majesty was young, he bore the screen and held court—his duty was like the partition of Shaan and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly recall our late lord, the Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe, who held the pivot of government and stood among those who counsel the throne, who served the public good with utter loyalty and gave his whole strength to the state. From the late emperor's death, when Your Majesty was still a child, he stood behind the screen and governed—the moral equivalent of the Duke of Zhou's regency.

sentences.zh: 宋維反常小子，性若青蠅，汙白點黑，讒佞是務，以元叉皇姨之壻，權勢攸歸，遂相附託，規求榮利，共結圖謀，坐生眉眼，誣告國王，枉以大逆。

translations.literal: Song Wei was an abnormal petty fellow, his nature like the green fly that soils white and spots black, devoted to slander and flattery. As Yuan Cha was the empress's nephew by marriage, power gravitated to him; they therefore attached to one another, schemed for glory and profit, jointly plotted, fabricated expressions, falsely accused the Prince of the state, and wrongly charged him with great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei was a vicious nobody, foul as the fly that soils what is white and blackens what is clean, devoted to slander and flattery. As Yuan Cha was the empress's nephew by marriage, power flowed to him; the two joined forces, schemed for advancement, invented evidence, and falsely accused the prince of high treason.

sentences.zh: 賴明明在上，赫赫臨下，泥漬自消，玉質還潔。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your bright clarity above and majestic presence below, mud stains vanished of themselves and jade quality returned to purity.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's luminous clarity and majestic authority, the mud has washed away of itself and the jade has regained its purity.

sentences.zh: 謹案律文：諸告事不實，以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the statutes: for all who report matters that are not true, punish them with the crime they alleged.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully cite the law: whoever lodges a false accusation shall be punished with the crime he alleged.

sentences.zh: 維遂無罪，出為大郡，刑賞僭差，朝野怪愕。

translations.literal: Yet Wei went without punishment and was sent out to a great commandery—punishment and reward were out of order, and court and countryside were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei went unpunished and was sent to govern a great commandery—rewards and punishments were grossly out of balance, and court and countryside alike were appalled.

sentences.zh: 若非宋維與叉為計，豈得全其身命，方撫千里？

translations.literal: If not for Song Wei and Cha plotting together, how could he have preserved his life and body and now rule a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: Had Song Wei not been acting in concert with Yuan Cha, how could he have escaped with his life and now be governing a great territory?

sentences.zh: 王以權在寵家，塵謗紛雜，恭慎之心，逾深逾厲，去其本宅，移住殿西，闔門靜守，親賓阻絕。

translations.literal: The Prince, because power lay in the favored clan and dust of slander swirled mixed, grew ever more respectful and cautious; he left his original residence, moved to dwell west of the hall, closed his gates in quiet guard, and kin and guests were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Because power lay with the favored faction and slander swirled about him, the prince grew ever more respectful and cautious; he left his own residence, moved to quarters west of the palace hall, kept his gates closed in quiet seclusion, and cut himself off from kin and guests.

sentences.zh: 于時，吏部諮禀劉騰，奏其弟官，郡戍兼補。

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Personnel consulted and reported to Liu Teng, memorializing an office for his younger brother and a garrison post in the commandery as a concurrent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Ministry of Personnel consulted Liu Teng and memorialized an appointment for the prince's younger brother, with a concurrent garrison post in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 及經內呈，為王駁退。

translations.literal: When it passed inward for presentation, the Prince rejected and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: When the proposal reached the inner court, the prince rejected it.

sentences.zh: 騰由此生嫌，私深怨怒，遂乃擅廢太后，離隔二宮，拷掠胡定，[1]誣王行毒，含齒戴髮，莫不悲惋。

translations.literal: Teng thereby conceived resentment and privately harbored deep anger; he then on his own authority deposed the Empress Dowager, separated the two palaces, tortured Hu Ding, [1] falsely accused the Prince of poisoning, and among all who bore teeth and hair none was not grieved and lamenting.
translations.idiomatic: Teng took offense at this and nursed a deep private grudge; he then arrogated to himself the deposing of the empress dowager, separated the two palaces, tortured Hu Ding, falsely accused the prince of poisoning, and every man and woman in the realm grieved.

sentences.zh: 及會公卿，議王之罪，莫不俛眉飲氣，唯諮是從。

translations.literal: When the high ministers assembled to deliberate the Prince's crime, none did not lower brows and swallow breath—only consultation was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the high ministers assembled to judge the prince's alleged crime, every man lowered his eyes and held his breath, daring only to echo what they were told.

sentences.zh: [2]僕射游肇，亢言厲氣，發憤成疾，為王致死。

translations.literal: [2] Vice Director You Zhao spoke forthrightly with stern spirit, fell ill from indignant rage, and died for the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director You Zhao alone spoke out boldly and with fierce resolve; he fell ill from righteous anger and died for the prince's sake.

sentences.zh: 王之忠誠款篤，節義純貞，非但蘊藏胸襟，實乃形於文翰，搜括史傳，撰顯忠錄，區目十篇，分卷二十。

translations.literal: The Prince's loyal sincerity was earnest and deep, his integrity and righteousness pure and true—not only stored in the breast but actually embodied in writings: he searched historical records and composed Records of Manifest Loyalty in ten sections across twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's loyalty was earnest and deep, his integrity pure—not merely held in his heart but set down in writing: he searched the historical records and compiled Records of Manifest Loyalty in ten sections across twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 既欲彰忠心於萬代，豈可為逆亂於一朝。

translations.literal: Since he wished to display loyal hearts for ten thousand generations, how could he commit rebellion in a single morning?
translations.idiomatic: A man who sought to proclaim loyal hearts for ten thousand generations could hardly have plotted rebellion in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 乞追遺志，足明丹款。

translations.literal: We beg to pursue his surviving intent—this suffices to clarify his red sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that his surviving writings be examined—they are proof enough of his loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 叉籍寵姻戚，恃握兵馬，無君之心，實懷皂白。

translations.literal: Cha relied on favor as an in-law, trusted in holding troops and horses, harbored a heart without a lord, and truly carried black and white reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha, relying on favor as the empress's kinsman and on his command of troops and horses, harbored a heart that acknowledged no sovereign and truly inverted right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 擅廢太后，枉害國王，生殺之柄，不由陛下，賞罰之詔，一出於叉。

translations.literal: He on his own authority deposed the Empress Dowager, wrongly harmed the Prince of the state; the power of life and death did not rest with Your Majesty, and edicts of reward and punishment issued solely from Cha.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed the empress dowager on his own authority and wrongfully destroyed the prince; the power of life and death no longer rested with Your Majesty, and orders of reward and punishment issued from Yuan Cha alone.

sentences.zh: 名藩重地，皆其親黨；

translations.literal: Famous fiefs and weighty territories were all his kin and partisans;
translations.idiomatic: Famous principalities and strategic territories were all given to his kin and partisans;

sentences.zh: 京官要任，必其心腹。

translations.literal: Important posts in the capital were always his trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Every important post at court went to his own men.

sentences.zh: 中山王熙，本興義兵，不圖神器，戮其大逆，合門滅盡，遂令元略南奔，為國巨患。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Zhongshan had originally raised righteous troops and did not covet the imperial regalia; yet they slaughtered him for great treason and exterminated his entire household, causing Yuan Lue to flee south and become a great peril to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Zhongshan had raised loyal troops without seeking the throne, yet they executed him for high treason and wiped out his whole clan, driving Yuan Lue south to become a grave menace to the realm.

sentences.zh: [3]奚康生國之猛將，盡忠棄市。

translations.literal: [3] Xi Kangsheng, a fierce general of the state, gave full loyalty yet was abandoned to the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Xi Kangsheng, one of the realm's fiercest generals, served with utter loyalty yet was cast out to public execution.

sentences.zh: 其餘枉被屠戮者，不可稱數。

translations.literal: The rest who were wrongly slaughtered cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The others wrongfully put to death are beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 緣此普天喪氣，匝地憤傷。

translations.literal: Because of this all under heaven lost spirit and the whole land was filled with angry grief.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the whole realm lost heart and grief and rage spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 致使朔隴猖狂，歷歲為亂，荊徐蠢動，職是之由。

translations.literal: This caused Shuofang and Longyou to run wild in rebellion year after year and Jing and Xu to stir in unrest—these troubles arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the northwest has raged in rebellion year after year and Jing and Xu have stirred in unrest.

sentences.zh: 昔趙高秉秦，令關東鼎沸；

translations.literal: In the past Zhao Gao held Qin and made the lands east of the passes boil like a cauldron;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhao Gao seized Qin and set the east ablaze;

sentences.zh: 今元叉執權，使四方雲擾。

translations.literal: now Yuan Cha holds power and makes the four quarters storm with trouble.
translations.idiomatic: today Yuan Cha holds power and throws the four quarters into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，竹帛所載，賊子亂臣，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, as recorded on bamboo and silk, among traitorous sons and rebellious ministers none has surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, in all that history records on bamboo and silk, no traitor or rebel minister has surpassed this.

sentences.zh: 開逆之始。

translations.literal: The beginning of opening rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The opening of rebellion began

sentences.zh: 起自宋維，成禍之末，良由騰矣。

translations.literal: arose from Song Wei; the completion of the disaster in the end was truly from Teng.
translations.idiomatic: with Song Wei; the disaster was brought to completion chiefly by Liu Teng.

sentences.zh: 而令凶徒姦黨，迭相樹置，高官厚祿，任情自取，非但臣等痛恨終身，抑為聖朝懷慚負愧。

translations.literal: Yet vicious fellows and treacherous factions are set up in turn, taking high offices and rich salaries as they please—not only do we hate this for life, but the sacred court itself must bear shame and guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these vicious men and treacherous factions are installed one after another, taking high office and rich salaries at will—not only do we hate this for life, but the sacred court itself must bear shame for it.

sentences.zh: 以臣赤心慺慺之見，宜梟諸兩觀，洿其舍廬。

translations.literal: In my loyal and earnest view, they should be displayed at the two gates and their dwellings defiled.
translations.idiomatic: In our loyal and earnest view, they should be exposed at the palace gates and their dwellings defiled.

sentences.zh: 騰合斵棺斬骸，沉其五族。

translations.literal: Teng should have his coffin broken open, his corpse cut down, and his five kin-groups drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng's coffin should be broken open, his corpse cut down, and his entire clan destroyed.

sentences.zh: 上謝天人幽隔之憤，下報忠臣冤酷之痛。

translations.literal: Above it would answer the anger of heaven and man separated in the dark; below it would repay the bitter wrongs of loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This would appease heaven's wrath above and repay loyal ministers' bitter wrongs below.

sentences.zh: 方乃崇亞三事，委以樞端，所謂虎也更傅其翼。

translations.literal: Yet now he is honored next to the Three Excellencies and entrusted with the pivot—this is what is called giving wings to a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Yuan Cha is honored next to the Three Excellencies and entrusted with the pivot of power—this is giving wings to a tiger.

sentences.zh: 朝野切齒，遐邇扼腕。

translations.literal: Court and countryside grind their teeth; near and far clench their fists.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside grind their teeth in rage; near and far clench their fists in helpless anger.

sentences.zh: 蔓草難除，去之宜盡。

translations.literal: Running weeds are hard to remove—they should be uprooted completely.
translations.idiomatic: Running weeds are hard to uproot—they must be removed to the last root.

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀曠代，緬追振古，當斷不斷，其禍更生。

translations.literal: I have surveyed distant ages and traced back to high antiquity: when one should cut but does not, disaster springs anew.
translations.idiomatic: We have surveyed distant ages and traced back to antiquity: when rulers fail to act decisively, disaster springs up again.

sentences.zh: 況叉猜忍，更居衡要。

translations.literal: How much more when Cha is suspicious and cruel and again holds the balance of power.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when Yuan Cha, suspicious and cruel, again holds the balance of power.

sentences.zh: 臣中宵九歎，竊以寒心，實願宸鑒，早為之所。

translations.literal: I sigh nine times in the middle of the night and secretly feel my heart grow cold; I truly wish Your Majesty's clear sight would act early.
translations.idiomatic: We sigh through the night and our hearts grow cold; we beg Your Majesty's clear sight to act before it is too late.

sentences.zh: 臣等潛伏閭閻，於茲六載，旦號白日，夕泣星辰，叩地寂寥，呼天無響。

translations.literal: We have lain hidden in our lanes for six years now, crying out by day to the white sun and weeping by night to the stars, knocking the earth in its silence and calling heaven without answer.
translations.idiomatic: We have lain hidden in our homes for six years, crying out by day to the sun and weeping by night to the stars, beating the silent earth and calling to heaven without answer.

sentences.zh: 衞野納肝，秦庭夜哭，千古之痛，何足相比。

translations.literal: Wei Yi's offering of his liver and the night weeping in the court of Qin—how can the pain of a thousand ages compare?
translations.idiomatic: The grief of Wei Yi offering his liver and the night weeping in the court of Qin scarcely compare with ours.

sentences.zh: 今幸遇陛下叡聖，親覽萬幾，太后仁明，更撫四海，臣等敢詣闕披陳，乞報冤毒。

translations.literal: Now we are fortunate to meet Your Majesty's sagely brilliance, personally reviewing the ten thousand affairs; the Empress Dowager is benevolent and clear, again comforting the four seas—we dare come to the gate to lay bare our plea and beg redress for poisonous wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are fortunate that Your Majesty's sagely brilliance personally governs the realm and the empress dowager's benevolent clarity again comforts the four seas; we dare come to the gate to lay bare our plea and beg redress for these poisonous wrongs.

sentences.zh: 書奏，靈太后義之，乃引子熙為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Dowager Ling approved its righteousness and summoned Zixi as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Empress Dowager Ling approved its righteousness and appointed Zixi Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後遂剖騰棺，賜叉死。

translations.literal: Later Teng's coffin was broken open and Cha was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Teng's coffin was broken open and Yuan Cha was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 尋修國史，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he compiled the national history and was given the additional title Pacification-North General.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took part in compiling the national history and was given the additional title Pacification-North General.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除著作郎，又兼司州別駕。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Compilation Gentleman and concurrently served as Sizhou Vice-Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Compilation Gentleman and concurrently served as vice-prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍、鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Support-the-State General and Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Support-the-State General and vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 建義初，兼黃門，尋正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he served concurrently in the Yellow Gate and soon received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he served concurrently in the Yellow Gate and soon received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 子熙清白自守，不交人事。

translations.literal: Zixi kept himself pure and aloof and did not mix in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi kept himself pure and aloof and did not mix in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 又少孤，為叔顯宗所撫養，及顯宗卒，顯宗子伯華又幼，子熙友愛，等於同生，長猶共居，車馬資財，隨其費用，未嘗見於言色。

translations.literal: He was also orphaned young and raised by his uncle Xianzong; when Xianzong died, Xianzong's son Bohua was still young. Zixi's brotherly love was like that of full brothers; even grown they still lived together, sharing carriages, horses, and property as needed without a word of complaint showing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle Xianzong; when Xianzong died, Xianzong's son Bohua was still a child. Zixi treated him with the devotion of a full brother; even as adults they lived together, sharing horses, carriages, and property as needed without a trace of resentment in word or manner.

sentences.zh: 又上書求析階與伯華，於是除伯華東太原太守。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial asking to divide his rank with Bohua; Bohua was then appointed Administrator of Eastern Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized asking to share his official rank with Bohua, who was then appointed administrator of Eastern Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及伯華在郡，為刺史元弼所辱，子熙乃泣訴朝廷，肅宗詔遣按檢，弼遂大見詰讓。

translations.literal: When Bohua was in the commandery and was insulted by Inspector Yuan Bi, Zixi wept and appealed to the court; Emperor Suzong ordered an investigation, and Bi was severely reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: When Bohua was insulted in his commandery by Inspector Yuan Bi, Zixi wept and appealed to the court; Emperor Suzong ordered an investigation, and Bi was severely reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之擒葛榮也，送至京師，莊帝欲面見數之。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong and sent him to the capital, Emperor Zhuang wished to see him face to face and rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong and sent him to the capital, Emperor Zhuang wished to see him face to face and rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 子熙以為榮既元兇，自知必死，恐或不遜，無宜見之。

translations.literal: Zixi thought that since Rong was the chief culprit and knew he must die, he might not be submissive and that it was not fitting to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi argued that as the chief culprit Ge Rong knew he must die and might not be submissive, so the emperor ought not see him.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮聞而大怒，請罪子熙，莊帝恕而不責。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong heard this and was greatly angered, requesting punishment for Zixi; Emperor Zhuang pardoned him without blame.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong heard this and was furious, demanding that Zixi be punished; Emperor Zhuang pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 尋加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Campaign-Barbarian General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional title Campaign-Barbarian General.

sentences.zh: 及邢杲之起逆，詔子熙慰勞。

translations.literal: When Xing Gao rose in rebellion, an edict ordered Zixi to console and encourage the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Gao rose in rebellion, an edict ordered Zixi to go and console the troops.

sentences.zh: 杲詐降，而子熙信之，還至樂陵，杲復反，子熙遂還。

translations.literal: Gao feigned surrender and Zixi believed him; returning to Leling, Gao rebelled again and Zixi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao feigned surrender and Zixi believed him; after returning to Leling, Gao rebelled again and Zixi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 坐付廷尉，論以大辟，恕死免官。

translations.literal: He was handed over to the Court of Justice, sentenced to the great punishment, but pardoned from death and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed over to the Court of Justice and sentenced to death, but was pardoned and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: Before long he served concurrently as Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he served concurrently as director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，除通直散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、光祿大夫，尋正吏部郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication, Pacification-Army General, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and soon received regular appointment as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Putai era he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication, Pacification-Army General, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and soon received regular appointment as director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，還領著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he again headed the Compilation Office as Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he again headed the historiographical office as Compilation Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 以奉冊之故，封歷城縣開國子，食邑五百戶，又加衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For presenting the imperial register he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Licheng with a fief of five hundred households and given the additional titles Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting the imperial register he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Licheng with a fief of five hundred households and given the additional titles Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 天平初，為侍讀，又除國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he served as Lecturer-in-Attendance and was appointed Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he served as lecturer-in-attendance and was appointed director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 子熙儉素安貧，常好退靜，遷鄴之始，百司並給兵力，時以祭酒閑務，止給二人。

translations.literal: Zixi was frugal and content in poverty and always loved retirement and quiet; at the beginning of the move to Ye, all offices were supplied with military retainers, but because the director's post was considered an idle duty, he was given only two men.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was frugal and content in poverty and always preferred retirement and quiet; at the beginning of the move to Ye every office was allotted military retainers, but because the academy directorship was considered a light post, he was given only two.

sentences.zh: 或有令其陳請者，子熙曰：「朝廷自不給祭酒兵，何關韓子熙事也。」

translations.literal: When someone urged him to petition for more, Zixi said: "If the court itself does not supply retainers to the academy director, what has that to do with Han Zixi?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to petition for more, Zixi said: "If the court itself does not supply retainers to the academy director, what has that to do with Han Zixi?"

sentences.zh: 論者高之。

translations.literal: Commentators esteemed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators esteemed him for this.

sentences.zh: 尋除驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 元象中，加衞大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was given the additional title Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was given the additional title Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 先是，子熙與弟娉王氏為妻，姑之女也，生二子。

translations.literal: Earlier Zixi had married his younger brother's wife, the Wang clan—a daughter of his aunt—and she bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zixi had betrothed a woman of the Wang clan, his aunt's daughter, as wife for his younger brother; she bore two sons.

sentences.zh: 子熙尚未婚，後遂與寡嫗李氏姦合而生三子。

translations.literal: Zixi himself was not yet married; later he had an illicit union with the widow Lady Li and she bore three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi himself was still unmarried; later he had an affair with the widow Lady Li, who bore three sons.

sentences.zh: 王李不穆，迭相告言，歷年不罷。

translations.literal: Wang and Li were not harmonious and accused each other in turn for years without end.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang and Lady Li were at odds and accused each other back and forth for years without end.

sentences.zh: 子熙因此慚恨，遂以發疾。

translations.literal: Zixi therefore felt shame and resentment and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was consumed with shame and resentment and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 興和中，孝靜欲行釋奠，敕子熙為侍講。

translations.literal: In Xinghe, Emperor Xiaojing wished to perform the libation sacrifice and ordered Zixi as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era Emperor Xiaojing wished to perform the libation sacrifice to Confucius and ordered Zixi to serve as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，遺戒不求贈諡，其子不能遵奉，遂至干謁。

translations.literal: He soon died, leaving instructions not to seek a posthumous title; his sons could not follow this and went so far as to lobby for one.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, leaving instructions not to seek a posthumous title; his sons could not obey and went so far as to lobby for one.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈驃騎將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was posthumously awarded Valiant Cavalry General, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was posthumously honored as Valiant Cavalry General, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 興宗弟顯宗，字茂親。

translations.literal: Xingzong's younger brother Xianzong, style Maoqin.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's younger brother was Xianzong, whose style was Maoqin.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，能面折庭諍，亦有才學。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and blunt; he could rebuke face to face in court debate and also had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and blunt by nature, able to rebuke others face to face at court, and possessed talent and learning as well.

sentences.zh: 沙門法撫，三齊稱其聰悟，常與顯宗校試，抄百餘人名，各讀一遍，隨即覆呼，法撫猶有一二舛謬，顯宗了無誤錯。

translations.literal: The monk Fafu, whom the three Qi regions praised for keen intelligence, often tested against Xianzong: they copied more than a hundred names, each read them once, then immediately called them back from memory. Fafu still had one or two errors; Xianzong had not a single mistake.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fafu, famed in the three Qi regions for his keen intelligence, often tested himself against Xianzong: they would copy more than a hundred names, read each list once, then immediately call them back from memory. Fafu still made one or two mistakes; Xianzong made none.

sentences.zh: 法撫歎曰：「貧道生平以來，唯服郎耳。」

translations.literal: Fafu sighed and said: "In all my poor monk's life I have admired only you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Fafu sighed and said: "In all my life as a monk I have admired only you, sir."

sentences.zh: 太和初，舉秀才，對策甲科，除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was recommended as Cultivated Talent, answered the policy questions in the top grade, and was appointed Assistant Compilation Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he was recommended as Cultivated Talent, ranked first in the policy examination, and was appointed Assistant Compilation Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 車駕南討，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he served concurrently as Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south he served concurrently as Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 既定遷都，顯宗上書：

translations.literal: Once the move of the capital was decided, Xianzong submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Once the move of the capital was decided, Xianzong submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 其一曰：竊聞輿駕今夏若不巡三齊，當幸中山，竊以為非計也。

translations.literal: The first point: I have heard that if the imperial carriage does not tour the three Qi this summer, it will visit Zhongshan—I humbly think this is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: First: I have heard that if Your Majesty does not tour the three Qi this summer, you will visit Zhongshan—I humbly believe this is unwise.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 當今徭役宜早息，洛京宜速成。

translations.literal: At present corvée labor should cease early and the Luo capital should be completed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor ought to cease as soon as possible and the Luo capital ought to be completed quickly.

sentences.zh: 省費則徭役可簡，并功則洛京易就。

translations.literal: If expenses are reduced, corvée can be lightened; if efforts are combined, the Luo capital is easy to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce expenses and corvée can be lightened; combine efforts and the Luo capital will be finished sooner.

sentences.zh: 往冬輿駕停鄴，是閑隙之時，猶編戶供奉，勞費為劇。

translations.literal: Last winter when the carriage halted at Ye—it was a time of leisure—registered households still supplied provisions and the labor and expense were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter, when the imperial progress halted at Ye—a time of relative leisure—registered households still had to supply provisions, and the burden was severe.

sentences.zh: 聖鑒矜愍，優旨殷勤，爵浹高年，賚周鰥寡，雖賑貸普霑，今猶恐來夏菜色。

translations.literal: Your sage sight was compassionate, your gracious edicts earnest; ranks reached the aged and gifts surrounded widows and orphans—though relief was widely bestowed, I still fear hunger-pale faces next summer.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's compassionate regard and gracious edicts reached the aged and surrounded widows and orphans with gifts—yet even though relief was widely distributed, I still fear wan faces next summer.

sentences.zh: [4]況三農要時，六軍雲會，其所損業，實為不少。

translations.literal: [4] How much more at the crucial season of the three agricultures, when the six armies gather like clouds—the livelihoods harmed will truly be no small number.
translations.idiomatic: [4] How much worse at the crucial season of agriculture, when the six armies gather like clouds—the damage to livelihoods will be considerable.

sentences.zh: 雖調斂輕省，未足稱勞，然大駕親臨，誰敢寧息？

translations.literal: Though levies may be lightened, that is not enough to be called easing labor—yet when the great carriage comes in person, who dares rest in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Even if levies are lightened, that scarcely counts as easing the burden—when the emperor comes in person, who dares rest?

sentences.zh: 往來承奉，紛紛道路，田蠶暫廢，則將來無資。

translations.literal: Coming and going in attendance, the roads in turmoil—fields and silkworms briefly abandoned—then the future will have no resources.
translations.idiomatic: With attendants coming and going and the roads in turmoil, fields and silkworms will be neglected—and then the future will have no resources.

sentences.zh: 此國之深憂也。

translations.literal: This is a deep worry for the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave worry for the state.

sentences.zh: 且向炎暑，而六軍暴露，恐生癘疫，此可憂之次也。

translations.literal: Moreover, facing scorching heat while the six armies are exposed—I fear pestilence may arise; this is the next cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in scorching heat the six armies will be exposed in the open—I fear pestilence may arise; this is the next worry.

sentences.zh: 臣願輿駕早還北京，以省諸州供帳之費，并功專力，以營洛邑。

translations.literal: I wish the imperial carriage would return early to the northern capital to save the supply costs of the various provinces and combine efforts in concentrated strength to build the Luo city.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty return early to the northern capital to save the provinces the cost of supplying the progress, and concentrate all effort on building the Luo capital.

sentences.zh: 則南州免雜徭之煩，北都息分析之歎，洛京可以時就，遷者僉爾如歸。

translations.literal: Then the southern provinces would be spared mixed corvée troubles, the northern capital would cease the sighs of division, the Luo capital could be completed on time, and those who relocate would all return as if going home.
translations.idiomatic: Then the southern provinces would be spared mixed corvée burdens, the northern capital would cease its laments over division, the Luo capital could be finished on schedule, and those who relocate would all come as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：自古聖帝必以儉約為美，亂主必以奢侈貽患。

translations.literal: The second point: from antiquity sage emperors have taken frugality as beautiful; chaotic rulers have brought disaster through extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Second: from antiquity sage emperors have prized frugality, while chaotic rulers have brought disaster through extravagance.

sentences.zh: 仰惟先朝，皆卑宮室而致力於經略，故能基宇開廣，業祚隆泰。

translations.literal: Looking up to the former court, all kept palaces low and devoted effort to statecraft, and therefore could broaden the foundation and make the enterprise lofty and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Our former emperors kept their palaces modest and devoted themselves to statecraft, and therefore broadened the foundation and secured a lofty inheritance.

sentences.zh: 今洛陽基址，魏明帝所營，取譏前代。

translations.literal: The present foundations of Luoyang were built by Emperor Ming of Wei and drew mockery from the previous age.
translations.idiomatic: The present foundations of Luoyang were built by Emperor Ming of Wei and drew mockery even in his own age.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下損之又損。

translations.literal: I bow and wish Your Majesty would reduce again and again.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to reduce them again and again.

sentences.zh: 頃來北都富室，競以第宅相尚，今因遷徙，宜申禁約，令貴賤有檢，無得踰制。

translations.literal: Recently in the northern capital wealthy houses competed in esteeming mansions; now because of the move, prohibitions should be announced so noble and humble have measure and none may exceed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Recently in the northern capital wealthy families competed in building grand mansions; with the move now at hand, prohibitions should be enforced so that noble and humble alike observe proper limits and none may exceed regulations.

sentences.zh: 端廣衢路，通利溝渠，使寺署有別，四民異居，永垂百世不刊之範，則天下幸甚矣。

translations.literal: Straighten and broaden the avenues, open and improve the canals, let temples and offices be distinct and the four classes dwell apart—if an unchanging model is left for a hundred generations, the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Straighten and broaden the avenues, open and improve the canals, let temples and offices be distinct and the four classes dwell apart—if an enduring model is left for a hundred generations, the realm will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 三曰：竊聞輿駕還洛陽，輕將數千騎。

translations.literal: The third point: I have heard that when the carriage returns to Luoyang it will take only a few thousand horsemen lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Third: I have heard that when Your Majesty returns to Luoyang you will travel with only a few thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 臣甚為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: I greatly disapprove of this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I strongly disapprove of this on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 夫千金之子，猶坐不垂堂，況萬乘之尊，富有四海乎？

translations.literal: A son worth a thousand gold pieces still does not sit with his mat hanging over the hall edge—how much more the lord of ten thousand chariots, rich in the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: A man worth a thousand gold pieces still will not sit where a tile might fall—how much more the Son of Heaven, who possesses the four seas?

sentences.zh: 警蹕於闈闥之內者，豈以為儀容而已，蓋以戒不虞也。

translations.literal: Imperial guards within the inner gates—is it only for display? It is to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guards within the palace gates are not mere display—they guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 清道而後行，尚恐銜蹶之或失，況履涉山河，而不加三思哉！

translations.literal: Even when the road is cleared before walking, one still fears the bit-horse may stumble—how much more when treading mountains and rivers without adding threefold thought!
translations.idiomatic: Even when the road is cleared beforehand one still fears the horse may stumble—how much more when crossing mountains and rivers without careful thought!

sentences.zh: 此愚臣之所以悚息，伏願少垂省察。

translations.literal: This is why your foolish minister trembles and breathes shallowly; I bow and wish you would bestow a little reflection.
translations.idiomatic: This is why your humble servant trembles with fear; I beg Your Majesty to reflect on this.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：伏惟陛下耳聽法音，目玩墳典，口對百辟，心虞萬幾，晷昃而食，夜分而寢。

translations.literal: The fourth point: I bow and reflect that Your Majesty's ears hear the sounds of law, your eyes peruse the classics, your mouth answers the hundred ministers, your mind worries over the ten thousand affairs—eating when the sundial slants, sleeping when night divides.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Your Majesty's ears hear the sounds of law, your eyes peruse the classics, your mouth answers the hundred ministers, your mind worries over ten thousand affairs—you eat when the sundial slants and sleep only after night has divided.

sentences.zh: 加以孝思之至，隨時而深；

translations.literal: Added to this, filial thought reaches its utmost and deepens with the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, filial devotion deepens with every season;

sentences.zh: 文章之業，日成篇卷。

translations.literal: literary work daily completes scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: and literary work daily completes new scrolls.

sentences.zh: 雖叡明所用，未足為煩，然非所以嗇神養性，頤無疆之祚。

translations.literal: Though used by sagely brilliance and not enough to be called trouble, this is not the way to spare the spirit and nurture one's nature and extend boundless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Though your sagely brilliance makes this no burden, it is not the way to spare the spirit, nurture your nature, and secure boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 莊周有言：形有待而智無涯，以有待之形，役無涯之智，殆矣。

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou said: the form has dependencies but wisdom has no boundary—using a dependent form to drive boundless wisdom is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zhou said: the body has limits but the mind has none—to drive a limited body with an unlimited mind is perilous.

sentences.zh: 此愚臣所不安，伏願陛下垂拱司契，委下責成，唯冕旒垂纊，而天下治矣。

translations.literal: This is what your foolish minister finds uneasy; I bow and wish Your Majesty would fold your hands and hold the tally, delegate below and assign responsibility—only the tasselled cap hanging down, and the realm would be governed.
translations.idiomatic: This is what troubles your humble servant; I beg Your Majesty to fold your hands in rule, delegate responsibility below, and let the tasselled cap hang down while the realm governs itself.

sentences.zh: 高祖頗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu largely accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen largely accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 顯宗又上言曰：「進賢求才，百王之所先也。

translations.literal: Xianzong again submitted a statement, saying: "Advancing the worthy and seeking talent is what the hundred kings put first.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong submitted another memorial, stating: "Advancing the worthy and seeking talent is what the hundred kings put first.

sentences.zh: 前代取士，必先正名，故有賢良、方正之稱。

translations.literal: Former ages in selecting scholars first rectified names, and therefore had the titles Worthy and Upright, and Upright and Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages, in selecting officials, first rectified names, and therefore had titles such as Worthy and Upright and Upright and Direct.

sentences.zh: 今之州郡貢察，徒有秀、孝之名，而無秀、孝之實。

translations.literal: Today's provincial and commandery recommendations and inspections have only the names Cultivated and Filial but not the reality of Cultivated and Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Today's provincial and commandery recommendations bear only the names Cultivated and Filial, without the reality of cultivated talent or filial virtue.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷但檢其門望，不復彈坐。

translations.literal: Yet the court only checks their family standing and no longer impeaches and punishes them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court only verifies their pedigree and no longer holds anyone accountable for fraud.

sentences.zh: 如此，則可令別貢門望，以敍士人，何假冒秀、孝之名也？

translations.literal: If so, one might as well have a separate recommendation of family standing to appoint scholar-officials—why borrow the names Cultivated and Filial?
translations.idiomatic: In that case, you might as well establish a separate recommendation track for pedigree and use it to appoint officials—why bother with the pretense of Cultivated and Filial titles at all?

sentences.zh: 夫門望者，是其父祖之遺烈，亦何益於皇家？

translations.literal: As for family standing, it is the lingering glory of one's fathers and grandfathers—what use is it to the imperial house?
translations.idiomatic: Family pedigree is nothing but the inherited renown of one's ancestors—what good does that do the throne?

sentences.zh: 益於時者，賢才而已。

translations.literal: What benefits the age is talented men alone.
translations.idiomatic: What the age needs is talent, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 苟有其才，雖屠釣奴虜之賤，聖皇不耻以為臣；

translations.literal: If he has talent, even if he is as lowly as a butcher, fisherman, slave, or captive, the sage emperor is not ashamed to make him a minister;
translations.idiomatic: If a man has talent, even one as humble as a butcher, fisherman, bondsman, or captive, the sage ruler will not hesitate to take him into service;

sentences.zh: 苟非其才，雖三后之胤，自墜於皂隸矣。

translations.literal: If he lacks talent, even a descendant of the Three Sage Kings will fall of himself into menial servitude.
translations.idiomatic: If he lacks talent, even a descendant of the Three Sage Kings will sink to the status of a menial.

sentences.zh: 是以大才受大官，小才受小官，各得其所，以致雍熙。

translations.literal: Therefore great talent receives great office, small talent receives small office, each gets his proper place, and harmony is attained.
translations.idiomatic: Great talent should fill great office, lesser talent lesser office—each in his proper place, until the realm knows peace and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 議者或云，今世等無奇才，不若取士於門。

translations.literal: Some who discuss the matter say that people of this age have no extraordinary talent, and it would be better to select scholars from noble families.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that no one in our generation has truly exceptional talent, and that it would be better to recruit officials from distinguished families.

sentences.zh: 此亦失矣。

translations.literal: This too is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: That view is mistaken as well.

sentences.zh: 豈可以世無周邵，便廢宰相而不置哉？

translations.literal: How can one because the age lacks a Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao abolish the chancellorship and leave it vacant?
translations.idiomatic: Would you abolish the office of chancellor altogether just because no Duke of Zhou or Duke of Shao walks the earth?

sentences.zh: 但當校其有寸長銖重者，即先敍之，則賢才無遺矣。」

translations.literal: One need only assess whoever has even an inch of merit or a grain of worth and appoint him first, and then no talent will be overlooked."
translations.idiomatic: One need only weigh whoever has even the smallest measure of merit and appoint him promptly—and no worthy talent will be left behind."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「夫帝皇所以居尊以御下者，威也；

translations.literal: He also said: "The reason an emperor occupies the highest place to govern those below is authority;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "An emperor holds the highest place and governs those below through authority;

sentences.zh: 兆庶所以徙惡以從善者，法也。

translations.literal: The reason the myriad common people turn from evil and follow good is law.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the myriad common people turn from wickedness and embrace goodness is law.

sentences.zh: 是以有國有家，必以刑法為治，生民之命，於是而在。

translations.literal: Therefore whoever has a state or a family must govern through penal law; the lives of the people depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds a state or a household must govern through law and punishment; the lives of the people depend on it.

sentences.zh: 有罪必罰，罰必當辜，則雖箠撻之刑，而人莫敢犯也。

translations.literal: If there is guilt it must be punished, and punishment must fit the crime—then even if the penalty is flogging, no one will dare to offend.
translations.idiomatic: When guilt is certain, punishment must follow, and punishment must fit the offense—then even if the penalty is no more than flogging, no one will dare to transgress.

sentences.zh: 有制不行，人得僥倖，則雖參夷之誅，不足以肅。

translations.literal: If regulations exist but are not enforced and people can rely on luck, then even the extermination of three clans is not enough to inspire awe.
translations.idiomatic: When rules exist but go unenforced and people can count on luck, even the extermination of three clans will not restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 自太和以來，未多坐盜棄市，[5]而遠近肅清。

translations.literal: Since the Taihe era, not many have been executed for theft at the market,[5] yet near and far have been purified.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe era, relatively few thieves have been executed in the public market,[5] yet order has been restored near and far.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，止姦在於防檢，不在麗刑也。

translations.literal: From this perspective, stopping wickedness lies in prevention and inspection, not in lavish punishments.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that suppressing crime depends on prevention and enforcement, not on ever harsher punishments.

sentences.zh: 今州郡牧守，邀當時之名，行一切之法；

translations.literal: Now provincial and commandery governors and prefects, seeking contemporary renown, apply draconian methods;
translations.idiomatic: Today provincial and commandery governors and prefects, chasing reputations of the moment, impose sweeping harsh measures;

sentences.zh: 臺閣百官，亦咸以深酷為無私，以仁恕為容盜。

translations.literal: The central offices and all officials likewise treat harsh severity as impartiality and benevolent forbearance as tolerance of crime.
translations.idiomatic: Central offices and officials everywhere treat brutal severity as proof of impartiality and humane leniency as indulgence of crime.

sentences.zh: 迭相敦厲，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: Urging one another on, this has become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Each office urging the next on, this has hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下居九重之內，視人如赤子；

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells within the ninefold palace and treats people like infants;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells deep within the palace and treats the people like infants;

sentences.zh: 百司分萬務之要，遇下如仇讎。

translations.literal: The hundred offices, handling the essentials of ten thousand affairs, treat those below like mortal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices, each handling vital affairs, treat those beneath them like mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 是則堯舜止一人，而桀紂以千百。

translations.literal: Thus Yao and Shun exist in one person alone, while Jie and Zhou exist in hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In effect there is only one Yao or Shun, but Jie and Zhou by the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 和氣不至，蓋由於此。

translations.literal: That harmonious qi does not arrive is probably because of this.
translations.idiomatic: That harmonious spirit never reaches the people—likely for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 書曰：『與其殺不辜，寧失不經。』

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'Better to err in excess than to execute the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'Better to err through excess than to put the innocent to death.

sentences.zh: 實宜敕示百僚，以惠元元之命。」

translations.literal: It truly fitting to instruct and show the hundred officials, to show favor to the lives of the common people."
translations.idiomatic: It would truly be fitting to instruct all officials accordingly, for the sake of the common people's lives."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「昔周王為犬戎所逐，東遷河洛，鎬京猶稱『宗周』，以存本也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Formerly the Zhou king was driven off by the Quan Rong and moved east to the Luo River region; Hao still was called 'Ancestral Zhou' to preserve the root.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In antiquity the Zhou king was driven off by the Quan Rong and moved east to the Luo River region; Hao was still called 'Ancestral Zhou' in order to preserve the original foundation.

sentences.zh: 光武雖曰中興，實自創革，西京尚置京尹，亦不廢舊。

translations.literal: Although Guangwu is called a restorer, he in fact founded anew; still the Western Capital retained a capital commandant, and the old was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Guangwu is called a restorer, he in fact founded a new order; still the Western Capital kept its capital commandant, and the old capital was not abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今陛下光隆先業，遷宅中土，稽古復禮，於斯為盛，豈若周漢，出於不得已哉。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty gloriously advances the prior enterprise, moved the capital to the Central Lands, and examined antiquity to restore rites—in this you surpass all; how can this be like Zhou and Han, which came from necessity?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has gloriously advanced the prior enterprise, moved the capital to the Central Lands, and looked to antiquity to restore ritual—an achievement greater than any before. How can this be compared with Zhou and Han, where relocation was born of necessity?

sentences.zh: 按春秋之義，有宗廟曰都，無則謂之邑，此不刊之典也。

translations.literal: According to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, where there is an ancestral temple it is called a capital; where there is not, it is called a settlement—this is an immutable canon.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, a place with an ancestral temple is called a capital; without one it is called a settlement—an immutable rule.

sentences.zh: 況北代宗廟在焉，山陵託焉，王業所基，聖躬所載，其為神鄉福地，實亦遠矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ancestral temples of Northern Dai are there, the imperial tombs are entrusted there, the royal enterprise was founded there, and the sacred person was nurtured there—as a divine homeland and blessed place, its merit is truly far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Northern Dai holds the ancestral temples, entrusts the imperial tombs, founded the royal enterprise, and nurtured Your Majesty's own person—as a sacred homeland and blessed ground, its significance is truly profound.

sentences.zh: 今便同之郡國，臣竊不安。

translations.literal: Now to treat it the same as ordinary commanderies and kingdoms—I, your subject, feel uneasy at heart.
translations.idiomatic: To treat it now as just another commandery or kingdom leaves me deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 愚謂代京宜建畿置尹，一如故事，崇本重舊，以光萬葉。」

translations.literal: I foolishly think the Dai capital should establish a capital region and appoint a commandant, just as in precedent, honoring the root and valuing the old, to glorify ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully suggest that the Dai capital should have a capital region established and a commandant appointed, following precedent—honoring the root and valuing the old, to glorify ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伏見洛京之制，居民以官位相從，不依族類。

translations.literal: He also said: "I humbly observe that in the regulations of Luoyang, residents are arranged according to official rank, not by clan or class.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I humbly observe that under Luoyang's regulations, residents are grouped by official rank rather than by clan or social class.

sentences.zh: 然官位非常，有朝榮而夕悴，則衣冠淪於厮竪之邑，臧獲騰於膏腴之里。

translations.literal: Yet official rank is not permanent; when one is honored in the morning and ruined by evening, the gentry sink into neighborhoods of menials, while bondservants rise into rich districts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet official rank is not permanent; when a man is honored in the morning and ruined by evening, the gentry sink into neighborhoods of menials while bondservants rise into the finest districts.

sentences.zh: 物之顛倒，或至於斯。

translations.literal: Things turned upside down can reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: The world turned upside down can reach this extreme.

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，必令四民異居者，欲其業定而志專。

translations.literal: The sage kings of old required the four classes of people to live apart so that their occupations would be settled and their minds focused.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old required the four classes of people to live apart so that each occupation would be settled and each mind focused.

sentences.zh: 業定則不偽，志專則不淫。

translations.literal: When occupation is settled there is no falsehood; when the mind is focused there is no dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: When occupation is settled, there is no pretense; when the mind is focused, there is no dissipation.

sentences.zh: 故耳目所習，不督而就；

translations.literal: Therefore what eye and ear grow accustomed to is achieved without supervision;
translations.idiomatic: What eye and ear grow accustomed to is mastered without supervision;

sentences.zh: 父兄之教，不肅而成。

translations.literal: The teaching of fathers and elder brothers is accomplished without severity.
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of fathers and elder brothers takes hold without harsh discipline.
