sentences.zh: 仰惟太祖道武皇帝創基撥亂，日不暇給，然猶分別士庶，不令雜居，伎作屠沽，各有攸處。

translations.literal: Looking up, I reflect that Emperor Daowu, who founded the state and quelled disorder, had no leisure day by day, yet still separated gentry and commoners, forbade mixed residence, and assigned artisans, butchers, and wine sellers each to their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on Emperor Daowu, who founded the state amid chaos and had scarcely a free hour in the day, he still separated gentry from commoners, forbade mixed residence, and assigned artisans, butchers, and wine sellers each to their proper place.

sentences.zh: 但不設科禁，賣買任情，販貴易賤，錯居混雜。

translations.literal: But because no statutory prohibitions were set, buying and selling followed whim, the costly was traded for the cheap, and residences became jumbled and mixed.
translations.idiomatic: But because no statutory prohibitions were imposed, buying and selling followed whim, the costly was traded for the cheap, and neighborhoods became jumbled and mixed.

sentences.zh: 假令一處彈箏吹笛，緩舞長歌；

translations.literal: Suppose in one place zithers are plucked and flutes blown, with leisurely dances and long songs;
translations.idiomatic: Suppose in one place zithers are plucked and flutes blown, with languid dances and long songs;

sentences.zh: 一處嚴師苦訓，誦詩講禮。

translations.literal: In another place stern teachers labor to instruct, reciting the Odes and expounding ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In another place stern teachers labor over their pupils, reciting the Odes and expounding ritual.

sentences.zh: 宣令童齓，任意所從，其走赴舞堂者萬數，往就學館者無一。

translations.literal: If children were told to follow their own choice, those rushing to the dance hall would number in the tens of thousands, while not one would go to the study hall.
translations.idiomatic: If children were told to follow their own inclination, tens of thousands would rush to the dance hall and not one would go to the study hall.

sentences.zh: 此則伎作不可雜居，士人不宜異處之明驗也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof that artisans must not live mixed together and that scholar-officials should not dwell in separate scattered places.
translations.idiomatic: This is clear proof that artisans must not live intermingled and that men of learning should dwell together rather than scattered apart.

sentences.zh: 故孔父云里仁之美，孟母弘三徙之訓，賢聖明誨，若此之重。

translations.literal: Therefore Master Kong spoke of the beauty of a benevolent neighborhood, and Mencius's mother glorified the lesson of the three moves—the wise and sage attach such weight to this teaching.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Master Kong praised the beauty of dwelling among the benevolent, and Mencius's mother honored the lesson of the three moves—the wise and sage treat such teaching with this weight.

sentences.zh: 今令伎作家習士人風禮，則百年難成；

translations.literal: If one now has artisan households learn the customs and rites of scholar-officials, it would take a hundred years to succeed;
translations.idiomatic: If artisan households are now made to learn the customs and rites of scholar-officials, a hundred years may not suffice;

sentences.zh: 令士人兒童効伎作容態，則一朝可得。

translations.literal: If one has the children of scholar-officials imitate the postures of artisans, it can be achieved in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: If the children of scholar-officials are made to imitate the postures of artisans, it can be done in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 是以士人同處，則禮教易興；

translations.literal: Therefore when scholar-officials dwell together, ritual teaching is easy to foster;
translations.idiomatic: When men of learning dwell together, ritual teaching is easily fostered;

sentences.zh: 伎作雜居，則風俗難改。

translations.literal: When artisans live intermingled, custom is hard to reform.
translations.idiomatic: When artisans live intermingled, custom is hard to change.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每選舉人士，則校其一婚一宦，以為升降，何其密也。

translations.literal: Whenever the court selects and recommends men, it scrutinizes a single marriage and a single office appointment for promotion or demotion—how strict this is!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court selects and recommends men, it scrutinizes a single marriage and a single office appointment to determine rank—how meticulous that is!

sentences.zh: 至於開伎作宦途，[6]得與膏粱華望接閤連甍，何其略也。

translations.literal: Yet as for opening the official path to artisans,[6] allowing them to share adjoining eaves with the fine-grained and illustrious families—how lax this is!
translations.idiomatic: Yet as for opening the official path to artisans,[6] allowing them to live eave to eave with noble-born families of the highest standing—how lax that is!

sentences.zh: 此愚臣之所惑。

translations.literal: This is what your foolish subject finds perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your humble subject finds perplexing.

sentences.zh: 今稽古建極，光宅中區，凡所徙居，皆是公地，分別伎作，在於一言，有何為疑，而闕盛美。」

translations.literal: Now in examining antiquity to establish the supreme norm and illuminating the Central Realm, all who have moved reside on public land; separating artisans requires only a word—what is there to doubt, and why neglect this great improvement?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, in examining antiquity to establish the supreme norm and illuminating the Central Realm, all who have moved reside on public land; separating artisans requires only a word of command—what is there to doubt, and why neglect so great an improvement?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自南偽相承，竊有淮北，欲擅中華之稱，且以招誘邊民，故僑置中州郡縣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the Southern usurpers succeeded one another, usurping possession of the region north of the Huai, wishing to monopolize the title of Central States and also to attract and entice frontier people, they provisionally established Central Province commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Since the Southern usurpers succeeded one another, holding the region north of the Huai, they wished to monopolize the title of Central States and entice frontier peoples, and so provisionally established Central Province commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 自皇風南被，仍而不改，凡有重名，其數甚眾。

translations.literal: Since imperial influence spread south, this has continued unchanged; duplicated names are extremely many.
translations.idiomatic: Since imperial influence spread south, this has continued unchanged; duplicated place names are now extremely numerous.

sentences.zh: 疑惑書記，錯亂區宇，非所以疆域物土，必也正名之謂也。

translations.literal: This confuses records and disarranges the territorial realm—it is not the way to demarcate lands and classify terrain; this is precisely what is meant by 'the rectification of names must come first.'
translations.idiomatic: This confuses the records and disarranges the territorial realm—it is no way to demarcate lands and classify terrain; this is precisely what is meant by 'the rectification of names must come first.'

sentences.zh: 愚以為可依地理舊名，一皆釐革。

translations.literal: I foolishly think one can follow the old geographical names and reform all of them.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully suggest that the old geographical names be followed and all of them reformed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 小者并合，大者分置。

translations.literal: Small ones should be merged; large ones should be subdivided.
translations.idiomatic: Small districts should be merged; large ones subdivided.

sentences.zh: 及中州郡縣，昔以戶少併省，今人口既多，亦可復舊。

translations.literal: As for Central Province commanderies and counties, which were formerly merged and abolished because households were few—now that the population is large, the old divisions can also be restored.
translations.idiomatic: As for Central Province commanderies and counties, which were formerly merged and abolished when households were few—now that the population has grown, the old divisions can be restored as well.

sentences.zh: [7]君人者，以天下為家，不得有所私也。

translations.literal: [7] One who rules the people takes all under Heaven as his home and must not show partiality.
translations.idiomatic: [7] One who rules the people takes all under Heaven as his home and must not show partiality.

sentences.zh: 故倉庫儲貯，以俟水旱之災，供軍國之用，至於有功德者，然後加賜。

translations.literal: Therefore storehouses are stocked to await floods and drought, and to supply the army and state; only when there is merit and virtue are additional grants added.
translations.idiomatic: Storehouses are stocked to await flood and drought and to supply the army and state; only when there is merit and virtue are additional grants made.

sentences.zh: 爰及末代，乃寵之所隆，賜賚無限。

translations.literal: By the late age, what favorites received was exalted, and gifts and grants were boundless.
translations.idiomatic: By the late age, what favorites received had grown exalted, and gifts and grants knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 自比以來，亦為太過。

translations.literal: Since then as well, this has been excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Since then as well, this has gone too far.

sentences.zh: 在朝諸貴，受祿不輕，土木被錦綺，僮妾厭粱肉，而復厚賚屢加，動以千計。

translations.literal: The nobles at court receive generous salaries; their buildings are draped in brocade and silk, their servants and concubines surfeit on fine grain and meat—yet heavy grants are repeatedly added, often running to thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The nobles at court already receive generous salaries; their buildings are draped in brocade and silk, their servants and concubines surfeit on fine grain and meat—yet heavy grants are repeatedly added, often running to the thousands.

sentences.zh: 若分賜鰥寡，贍濟實多。

translations.literal: If distributed instead to widowers and widows, the relief would truly be great.
translations.idiomatic: If distributed instead to widowers and widows, the relief would be far greater.

sentences.zh: 如不悛革，豈周急不繼富之謂也？

translations.literal: If this is not reformed, is this not the opposite of 'aid the urgent, not enrich the already wealthy'?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not reformed, is this not the very opposite of 'aid the urgent, not enrich the already wealthy'?

sentences.zh: [8]愚謂事有可賞，則明旨褒揚，稱事加賜，以勸為善，不可以親近之昵，猥損天府之儲。」

translations.literal: [8] I foolishly think that when something deserves reward, let a clear edict praise it and add grants commensurate with the deed to encourage good conduct—you must not, out of intimacy with favorites, rashly drain the imperial treasury's stores."
translations.idiomatic: [8] I respectfully suggest that when something deserves reward, let a clear edict praise it and add grants commensurate with the deed to encourage good conduct—you must not, out of intimacy with favorites, rashly drain the imperial treasury."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「諸宿衞內直者，宜令武官習弓矢，文官諷書傳。

translations.literal: He also said: "All palace guards on internal duty should have military officers practice bows and arrows, and civil officers recite the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "All palace guards on internal duty should have military officers practice the bow and civil officers recite the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 而今給其蒱博之具，以成褻狎之容，長矜爭之心，恣諠囂之慢，徒損朝儀，無益事實。

translations.literal: Yet now they are supplied with gambling equipment, fostering an air of coarse familiarity, nurturing contentious pride, and indulging clamorous disrespect—they only harm court decorum and benefit nothing in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now they are supplied with gambling equipment, fostering an air of coarse familiarity, nurturing contentious pride, and indulging clamorous disrespect—they only harm court decorum and serve no practical purpose.

sentences.zh: 如此之類，一宜禁止。」

translations.literal: Matters of this kind should all be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Matters of this kind should all be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 高祖善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen approved of this.

sentences.zh: 後乃啟乞宋王劉昶府諮議參軍事，欲立効南境，高祖不許。

translations.literal: Later he submitted a request for the post of consulting adjutant on the staff of the Prince of Song, Liu Chang, wishing to render service on the southern frontier; Emperor Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted a request for the post of consulting adjutant on the staff of the Prince of Song, Liu Chang, wishing to render service on the southern frontier; Emperor Xiaowen did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾謂顯宗及程靈虬曰：「著作之任，國書是司。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once said to Xianzong and Cheng Lingqiu: "The charge of compilation is to manage the state chronicle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once said to Xianzong and Cheng Lingqiu: "The charge of compilation is to manage the state chronicle.

sentences.zh: 卿等之文，朕自委悉，中省之品，卿等所聞。

translations.literal: Your writings—I myself know them thoroughly; the appraisals of the inner secretariat—you have heard them.
translations.idiomatic: Your writings—I know them thoroughly myself; the appraisals of the inner secretariat—you have heard them.

sentences.zh: 若欲取況古人，班馬之徒，固自遼闊。

translations.literal: If one wishes to compare with the ancients, the likes of Ban and Sima are naturally far removed.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to compare with the ancients, the likes of Ban Gu and Sima Qian are naturally far beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 若求之當世，文學之能，卿等應推崔孝伯。」

translations.literal: If one seeks within the present age for literary ability, you should rank Cui Xiaobo first.
translations.idiomatic: If one seeks literary ability in the present age, you should rank Cui Xiaobo first.

sentences.zh: 又謂顯宗曰：「見卿所撰燕志及在齊詩詠，大勝比來之文。

translations.literal: He also said to Xianzong: "Having seen what you compiled, the Yan Chronicles, and your poetic compositions from your time in Qi, they far surpass your recent writings.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Xianzong: "Having seen your Yan Chronicles and the poems you wrote while in Qi, they far surpass your recent writings.

sentences.zh: 然著述之功，我所不見，當更訪之監、令。

translations.literal: Yet the merit of your compilations I have not seen myself; I must inquire further of the director and chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have not seen the merit of your compilations myself; I must inquire further of the director and chief.

sentences.zh: 校卿才能，可居中第。」

translations.literal: Judging your talent, you can be placed in the middle rank.
translations.idiomatic: Judging your talent, you can be placed in the middle rank.

sentences.zh: 又謂程靈虬曰：「卿比顯宗復有差降，可居下上。」

translations.literal: He also said to Cheng Lingqiu: "Compared with Xianzong you rank somewhat lower; you can occupy the lower-middle rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Cheng Lingqiu: "Compared with Xianzong you rank somewhat lower; you can be placed in the lower-middle rank.

sentences.zh: 顯宗對曰：「臣才第短淺，猥聞上天，至乃比於崔光，實為隆渥。

translations.literal: Xianzong replied: "Your subject's talent and rank are shallow and slight; to presumptuously hear the words of Heaven, and even to be compared with Cui Guang, is truly overwhelming favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong replied: "Your subject's talent and rank are shallow and slight; to hear the words of Heaven at all is presumptuous enough, and to be compared with Cui Guang is truly overwhelming favor.

sentences.zh: 然臣竊謂陛下貴古而賤今，臣學微才短，誠不敢仰希古人，然遭聖明之世，覩惟新之禮，染翰勒素，實錄時事，亦未慚於後人。

translations.literal: Yet your subject privately thinks that Your Majesty values the ancient and undervalues the present. My learning is slight and my talent limited—I truly dare not look up to the ancients. Yet having encountered a sage and enlightened age, witnessed renewing rites, taken brush to record on plain silk the events of the time, I would not yet feel ashamed before posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your subject privately thinks that Your Majesty values the ancient and undervalues the present. My learning is slight and my talent limited—I truly dare not aspire to the ancients. Yet having encountered a sage and enlightened age, witnessed renewing rites, and taken brush to plain silk to record the events of the time, I would not yet feel ashamed before posterity.

sentences.zh: 昔揚雄著太玄經，當時不免覆盎之談，二百年外，則越諸子。

translations.literal: Formerly Yang Xiong wrote the Classic of Supreme Mystery; at the time he could not escape talk of a covered jar, but two hundred years later he surpassed the various masters.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yang Xiong wrote the Classic of Supreme Mystery; at the time he could not escape talk of a covered jar, but two hundred years later he surpassed all the other masters.

sentences.zh: 今臣之所撰，雖未足光述帝載，稗暉日月，然萬祀之後，仰觀祖宗巍巍之功，上覩陛下明明之德，亦何謝欽明於唐典，慎徽於虞書。」

translations.literal: What your subject has compiled, though insufficient to gloriously set forth the imperial record or add even a grain of light to sun and moon, yet ten thousand generations hence, looking up to the towering achievements of the ancestors and above to Your Majesty's luminous virtue—why should it be inferior to reverent brilliance in the Documents of Tang, or careful virtue in the Documents of Yu?
translations.idiomatic: What your subject has compiled, though insufficient to gloriously set forth the imperial record or add even a grain of light to sun and moon, yet ten thousand generations hence, looking up to the towering achievements of the ancestors and above to Your Majesty's luminous virtue—why should it fall short of reverent brilliance in the Documents of Tang, or careful virtue in the Documents of Yu?

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「假使朕無愧於虞舜，卿復何如於堯臣？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Suppose I am not unworthy of Emperor Shun—how then do you compare with the ministers of Yao?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Suppose I am not unworthy of Emperor Shun—how then do you compare with the ministers of Yao?

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「臣聞君不可以獨治，故設百官以贊務。

translations.literal: Xianzong said: "Your subject has heard that a ruler cannot govern alone, and therefore the hundred offices were established to assist in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said: "Your subject has heard that a ruler cannot govern alone, and therefore the hundred offices were established to assist in affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下齊蹤堯舜，公卿寧非二八之儔。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty matches Yao and Shun in your track; are the ministers and high officials not the peers of the Two Assistants and Eight Worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty walks in the footsteps of Yao and Shun; are the ministers and high officials not the peers of the Two Assistants and Eight Worthies?

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿為著作，僅名奉職，未是良史也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "You serve as compiler in name only—you are not yet a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "You serve as compiler in name only—you are not yet a good historian.

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「臣仰遭明時，直筆而無懼，又不受金，安眠美食，此臣優於遷固也。」

translations.literal: Xianzong said: "Your subject has fortunately encountered an enlightened age, writes with a straight brush without fear, and accepts no gold—I sleep in peace and eat well. In this your subject surpasses Qian and Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said: "Your subject has fortunately encountered an enlightened age, writes with a straight brush without fear, and accepts no bribes—I sleep in peace and eat well. In that respect your subject surpasses Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 高祖哂之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu smiled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen smiled at this.

sentences.zh: 後與員外郎崔逸等參定朝儀。

translations.literal: Later he joined Adjunct Officer Cui Yi and others in fixing court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Adjunct Officer Cui Yi and others in drafting court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾詔諸官曰：「自近代已來，高卑出身，恒有常分。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once issued an edict to the officials, saying: "Since recent times, high and low in origin have always had fixed divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once issued an edict to the officials, saying: "Since recent times, high and low in origin have always had fixed divisions.

sentences.zh: 朕意一以為可，復以為不可。

translations.literal: My mind at one time finds this acceptable, at another unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: At one moment my mind finds this acceptable, at the next unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 宜相與量之。」

translations.literal: You should measure this together among yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: You should weigh this together.

sentences.zh: 李沖對曰：「未審上古已來，置官列位，為欲為膏粱兒地，為欲益治讚時？」

translations.literal: Li Chong replied: "I do not yet know whether, from high antiquity onward, offices and ranks were established to carve out positions for the sons of noble families, or to benefit governance and assist the age?
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong replied: "I do not yet know whether, from high antiquity onward, offices and ranks were established to carve out positions for the sons of noble families, or to benefit governance and assist the age?

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「俱欲為治。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Both were meant for governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Both were meant for governance.

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「若欲為治，陛下今日何為專崇門品，不有拔才之詔？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "If the aim is governance, why does Your Majesty today exclusively exalt family rank, without an edict to elevate talent?
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong said: "If the aim is governance, why does Your Majesty today exclusively exalt family rank, without an edict to elevate talent?

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「苟有殊人之伎，不患不知。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "If one has extraordinary human skill, one need not worry about not being known.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If a man has extraordinary talent, he need not fear going unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 然君子之門，假使無當世之用者，要自德行純篤，朕是以用之。」

translations.literal: Yet in a gentleman's house, even if there is one without immediate usefulness for the age, as long as virtue and conduct are pure and sincere, I therefore employ him."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a gentleman's household, even when someone lacks immediate use for the times, if his virtue and conduct are pure and steadfast, that is reason enough for me to employ him."

sentences.zh: 沖曰：「傅巖、呂望，豈可以門見舉？」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Fu Yan and Lü Wang — could they have been recommended on the basis of family rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong said: "Fu Yue of Fu Cliff and Lü Wang — were they ever raised up because of their family rank?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「如此濟世者希，曠代有一兩人耳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Such world-saving men are rare; across an age there may be one or two."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Men who can save the age are rare — an era may produce only one or two."

sentences.zh: 沖謂諸卿士曰：「適欲請諸賢救之。」

translations.literal: Chong said to the ministers and worthies: "I was just about to ask you worthies to rescue this."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong said to the assembled ministers and worthies: "I was on the point of asking you gentlemen to save the argument."

sentences.zh: 祕書令李彪曰：「師旅寡少，未足為援，意有所懷，不敢盡言於聖日。

translations.literal: Secretary Director Li Biao said: "Our allies are few and cannot serve as support; I have thoughts in my heart but dare not speak them fully on this sacred day.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Li Biao said: "Our allies are too few to lend weight to the debate; I have something in mind, but dare not speak it fully before Your Majesty on this august day.

sentences.zh: 陛下若專以門地，不審魯之三卿，孰若四科？」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty relies solely on family status, I do not know — compared with the three ranks of Lu, how do they match the Four Categories?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty relies solely on family status, I ask: compared with the three ministerial houses of Lu, how do they measure against Confucius's Four Categories?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「猶如向解。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "As explained before."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "As I explained earlier."

sentences.zh: 顯宗進曰：「陛下光宅洛邑，百禮唯新，國之興否，指此一選。

translations.literal: Xianzong stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty has gloriously taken residence in Luoyang; all rites are renewed — the rise or fall of the state hinges on this selection.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty has gloriously established the capital at Luoyang, and every rite is being made anew; the fate of the state turns on this one choice of men.

sentences.zh: 臣既學識浮淺，不能援引古今，以證此議，且以國事論之。

translations.literal: Your subject's learning is shallow; I cannot cite antiquity and the present to prove this argument — I shall discuss it in terms of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: My own learning is shallow, and I cannot summon antiquity and the present to prove this point; let me speak instead from the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 不審中、祕書監令之子，必為祕書郎，頃來為監、令者，子皆可為不？」

translations.literal: I do not know — must the sons of central and secretariat supervisors and directors necessarily become secretariat gentlemen? In recent times, have all sons of those who served as supervisors and directors been qualified?"
translations.idiomatic: I ask: must the sons of central and secretariat supervisors and directors inevitably become secretariat gentlemen? In recent years, have all the sons of men appointed supervisor or director truly been fit for the post?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿何不論當世膏腴為監、令者？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Why do you not discuss the rich and noble families who serve as supervisors and directors in our age?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Why do you not speak of the wealthy and eminent families who hold the posts of supervisor and director today?"

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「陛下以物不可類，不應以貴承貴，以賤襲賤。」

translations.literal: Xianzong said: "Your Majesty holds that things cannot be grouped alike; one should not have the noble inherit noble rank, the base inherit base rank."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said: "Your Majesty holds that things cannot be lumped together; one ought not have the noble inherit nobility, or the base inherit baseness."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「若有高明卓爾、才具雋出者，朕亦不拘此例。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "If there is one who is brilliant and outstanding, whose talent is extraordinary, I also do not hold to this rule."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If someone is brilliant and outstanding, with talent that rises above the rest, I do not bind myself to this rule either."

sentences.zh: 後為本州中正。

translations.literal: Later he was made Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，車駕南伐，顯宗為右軍府長史、征虜將軍、統軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when the emperor marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 軍次赭陽，蕭鸞戍主成公期遣其軍主胡松、高法援等并引蠻賊來擊軍營，顯宗親率拒戰，遂斬法援首。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Zheyang, Xiao Luan's garrison commander Cheng Gongqi sent his army commanders Hu Song, Gao Fayuan, and others, together leading tribal raiders to attack the camp; Xianzong personally led the resistance and beheaded Fayuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Zheyang, Cheng Gongqi, garrison commander under Xiao Luan, sent his commanders Hu Song and Gao Fayuan, among others, together with tribal allies to strike the camp; Xianzong personally led the defense and cut off Fayuan's head.

sentences.zh: 顯宗至新野，高祖詔曰：「卿破賊斬帥，殊益軍勢，朕方攻堅城，何為不作露布也？」

translations.literal: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Gaozu edicted: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening army morale; I am assaulting a fortified city — why did you not issue a battle report?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Xiaowen sent an edict: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening our army's momentum; I am pressing a hard siege — why did you not publish a victory bulletin?"

sentences.zh: 顯宗曰：「臣頃聞鎮南將軍王肅獲賊二三，驢馬數匹，皆為露布，臣在東觀，私每哂之。

translations.literal: Xianzong said: "Your subject recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and several donkeys and horses, yet issued battle reports; when I was at the Eastern Hall for observations, I privately always laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong said: "I recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and a few donkeys and horses, yet still issued victory bulletins; when I served at the Eastern Hall, I privately laughed at that every time.

sentences.zh: 近雖仰憑威靈，得摧醜虜，兵寡力弱，擒斬不多。

translations.literal: Recently, though relying on your august power I was able to crush the foul enemy, our troops were few and strength weak; captures and kills were not many.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though I leaned on your august power and was able to break the foul enemy, my troops were few and my strength slight; captures and kills were not many.

sentences.zh: 脫復高曳長縑，虛張功捷，尤而效之，其罪彌甚。

translations.literal: If I again hoisted long silk banners and falsely inflated achievements, committing the same fault and imitating that example, my guilt would be all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: If I now unfurled long silk banners and falsely inflated my achievements, copying that fault and making it my own, my offense would be all the graver.

sentences.zh: 臣所以斂毫卷帛，解上而已。」

translations.literal: Therefore I folded my brush and rolled up the silk and submitted a simple report, nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I put away brush and silk and submitted only a plain report."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「如卿此勳，誠合茅社，須赭陽平定，檢審相酬。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu smiled and said: "For merit such as yours, you truly deserve a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review and reward you accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen smiled and said: "Merit such as yours truly deserves a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review the matter and reward you properly."

sentences.zh: 新野平，以顯宗為鎮南、廣陽王嘉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was made consulting adjutant to Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was appointed consulting adjutant on the staff of Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 顯宗後上表，頗自矜伐，訴前征勳，詔曰：「顯宗斐然成章，甚可怪責，進退無檢，虧我清風。

translations.literal: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather self-praising, pleading his prior campaign merit. An edict read: "Xianzong's polished composition is much to be blamed; his advance and retreat lack restraint and damage our pure ethos.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather full of self-praise, pleading his earlier campaign merit. An edict said: "Xianzong's polished prose is very much to be censured; his conduct lacks restraint in advance and retreat, and it tarnishes our pure ethos.

sentences.zh: 此而不糾，或長弊俗。

translations.literal: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may grow.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may take deeper root.

sentences.zh: 可付尚書，推列以聞。」

translations.literal: Let it be referred to the Masters of Writing to investigate and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter be referred to the Masters of Writing for investigation and report."

sentences.zh: 兼尚書張彝奏免顯宗官，詔曰：「顯宗雖浮矯致愆，才猶可用，豈得永棄之也！

translations.literal: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity caused fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be abandoned forever!
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity brought him to fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be cast off forever!

sentences.zh: 可以白衣守諮議，展其後效。

translations.literal: He may serve as adviser in plain clothes and show his merit hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: He may continue as adviser in plain clothes and prove his worth hereafter.

sentences.zh: 但鄙很之性，不足參華，可奪見□，并禁問訊諸王。」

translations.literal: But his boorish and obstinate nature is unfit for elegant company; his audience privilege may be revoked □, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."
translations.idiomatic: But his coarse and obstinate nature makes him unfit for elegant company; his privilege of audience may be revoked, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."

sentences.zh: 顯宗既失意，遇信向洛，乃為五言詩贈御史中尉李彪曰：「賈生謫長沙，董儒詣臨江。

translations.literal: Disappointed, when the imperial missive arrived directing him toward Luoyang, Xianzong composed a five-character poem for Li Biao, Vice Censor, saying: "Jia Yi was banished to Changsha; Master Dong went to Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Disappointed in office, when orders came directing him toward Luoyang, Xianzong composed a five-character poem for Li Biao, Vice Censor, saying: "Jia Yi was exiled to Changsha; Dong Zhongshu went to Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 愧無若人跡，忽尋兩賢蹤。

translations.literal: Ashamed that I lack the footprints of such men, I suddenly find the traces of two worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that I lack the footprints of such men, I suddenly find myself walking in the traces of two sages.

sentences.zh: 追昔渠閣游，策駑厠羣龍。

translations.literal: Recalling our past companionship at the canal pavilion, I drove my sorry nag to stand among dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling our old companionship at the library pavilion, I drove my sorry nag to stand among dragons.

sentences.zh: 如何情願奪，飄然獨遠從？

translations.literal: How has desire been torn away, that I drift alone on a distant posting?
translations.idiomatic: How was my heart's wish torn away, that I drift alone on a distant posting?

sentences.zh: 痛哭去舊國，銜淚届新邦。

translations.literal: Weeping I leave the old land; tears in mouth I arrive at the new realm.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, I leave the old country; holding back tears, I arrive in a new land.

sentences.zh: 哀哉無援民，嗷然失侶鴻。

translations.literal: Alas, the unaided people cry out like a lonely goose bereft of its mate.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the people left without aid — they cry out like a goose that has lost its mate.

sentences.zh: 彼蒼不我聞，千里告志同。」

translations.literal: Heaven does not hear me; across a thousand li I declare our kindred spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven does not hear me; across a thousand li I declare that our hearts are one."

sentences.zh: 二十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died.

sentences.zh: 顯宗撰馮氏燕志，孝友傳各十卷，所作文章，頗傳於世。

translations.literal: Xianzong compiled the Annals of Yan of the Feng clan and Filial Piety and Friendship, ten scrolls each; his writings circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong compiled the Annals of Yan of the Feng clan and Filial Piety and Friendship, ten scrolls each; his writings circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 景明初，追赭陽勳，賜爵章武男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, his merit at Zheyang was posthumously honored with the title Baron of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, his merit at Zheyang was posthumously honored with the title Baron of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 子武華，襲。

translations.literal: His son Wuhua inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuhua inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除討寇將軍、奉朝請、太原太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Punishes Bandits, Attendant at Court, and Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Punishes Bandits, Attendant at Court, and Administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 程駿，字驎駒，本廣平曲安人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Jun, style Linju, was originally a native of Qu'an in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jun, style Linju, was originally from Qu'an in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 六世祖良，晉都水使者，坐事流于涼州。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Liang was Jin Director of Waterworks; punished for an offense, he was exiled to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Liang served as Jin Director of Waterworks; punished for an offense, he was exiled to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖父肇，呂光民部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Minister of the People under Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao was Minister of the People under Lü Guang.

sentences.zh: 駿少孤貧，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: Jun was orphaned young and poor; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was orphaned young and poor; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 師事劉昞，性機敏好學，晝夜無倦。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Bing; quick-witted and fond of learning, day and night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Bing; quick-witted and devoted to learning, he toiled day and night without weariness.

sentences.zh: 昞謂門人曰：「舉一隅而以三隅反者，此子亞之也。」

translations.literal: Bing told his disciples: "One who is shown one corner and returns with the other three — this youth ranks next to such."
translations.idiomatic: Bing told his disciples: "One who is shown one corner and infers the other three — this youth ranks next to such a man."

sentences.zh: 駿謂昞曰：「今世名教之儒，咸謂老莊其言虛誕，不切實要，弗可以經世，駿意以為不然。

translations.literal: Jun said to Bing: "Confucian scholars of the age all hold Laozi and Zhuangzi's words empty and false, not grounded in practical essentials, unfit to govern the world — I think otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said to Bing: "Confucian scholars of the age all hold that Laozi and Zhuangzi speak empty and false words, ungrounded in practical essentials and unfit to govern the world — I do not think so.

sentences.zh: 夫老子著抱一之言，莊生申性本之旨，若斯者，可謂至順矣。

translations.literal: Laozi wrote on embracing unity; Master Zhuang expounded the original nature of things — such teachings may be called perfectly harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi wrote on embracing unity; Master Zhuang expounded the original nature of things — teachings such as these may be called perfectly harmonious.

sentences.zh: 人若乖一則煩偽生，若爽性則沖真喪。」

translations.literal: When men depart from unity, fuss and falsehood arise; when they violate their nature, pure truth is lost."
translations.idiomatic: When men depart from unity, fuss and falsehood arise; when they violate their nature, pure truth is lost."

sentences.zh: 昞曰：「卿年尚稚，言若老成，美哉！」

translations.literal: Bing said: "You are still young, yet speak like a seasoned elder — splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: Bing said: "You are still young, yet speak like a seasoned elder — splendid!"

sentences.zh: 由是聲譽益播，沮渠牧犍擢為東宮侍講。

translations.literal: Thereupon his fame spread further; Juqu Mujian promoted him to lecturer in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his reputation spread further, and Juqu Mujian promoted him to lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太延五年，世祖平涼，遷于京師，為司徒崔浩所知。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiyan, Emperor Shizu pacified Liangzhou; he moved to the capital and came to the notice of Minister Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiyan, after Emperor Shizu pacified Liangzhou, he moved to the capital and came to the notice of Minister Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，拜著作佐郎，未幾，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he was appointed Associate Master of Letters; soon after, he was promoted to Master of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng acceded, he was appointed Associate Master of Letters; soon after, he was promoted to Master of Letters.

sentences.zh: 為任城王雲郎中令，進箴於王，王納而嘉之。

translations.literal: As Director of the Palace for Prince Yun of Chengyun, he presented admonitions to the prince, who accepted and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of the Palace for Prince Yun of Chengyun, he presented admonitions to the prince, who accepted and praised them.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，除高密太守。

translations.literal: During Huangxing, he was appointed Administrator of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangxing, he was appointed Administrator of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 尚書李敷奏曰：「夫君之使臣，必須終效。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Li Fu memorialized: "When a ruler employs a minister, he must complete his service.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Li Fu memorialized: "When a ruler employs a minister, the minister must see his charge through to the end.

sentences.zh: 駿實史才，方申直筆，千里之任，十室可有。

translations.literal: Jun is truly a historical talent, now wielding the straight brush; for the charge of a thousand li, one in ten households could suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Jun is truly a historian's talent, now wielding the straight brush; for the charge of a thousand li, one man in ten households would suffice.

sentences.zh: 請留之數載，以成前籍，後授方伯，愚以為允。」

translations.literal: Please retain him several years to complete the prior records; afterward appoint him regional governor — I deem this acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Please retain him several years to complete the earlier records; afterward appoint him regional governor — I deem this acceptable."

sentences.zh: 書奏，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 顯祖屢引駿與論易老之義，顧謂羣臣曰：「朕與此人言，意甚開暢。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu repeatedly summoned Jun to discuss the meanings of the Changes and Laozi, and turning to the ministers said: "When I speak with this man, my mind opens freely."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu repeatedly summoned Jun to discuss the meanings of the Changes and Laozi, and turning to the ministers said: "When I speak with this man, my mind opens freely."

sentences.zh: 又問駿曰：「卿年幾何？」

translations.literal: He also asked Jun: "How old are you?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Jun: "How old are you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣六十有一。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is sixty-one."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your subject is sixty-one."

sentences.zh: 顯祖曰：「昔太公既老而遭文王。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu said: "In olden days Taigong was already aged when he met King Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu said: "In olden days Taigong was already aged when he met King Wen.

sentences.zh: 卿今遇朕，豈非早也？」

translations.literal: You now meet me — is this not early?"
translations.idiomatic: You now meet me — is this not early?"

sentences.zh: 駿曰：「臣雖才謝呂望，而陛下尊過西伯。

translations.literal: Jun said: "Though my talent falls short of Lü Wang, Your Majesty's honor surpasses the Western Earl.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Though my talent falls short of Lü Wang, Your Majesty's honor surpasses the Western Earl.

sentences.zh: 覬天假餘年，竭六韜之効。」

translations.literal: I hope Heaven grants me remaining years to exhaust the efficacy of the Six Strategies."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Heaven grants me remaining years to exhaust the efficacy of the Six Strategies."

sentences.zh: 延興末，高麗王璉求納女於掖庭，顯祖許之，假駿散騎常侍，賜爵安豐男，加伏波將軍，持節如高麗迎女，賜布帛百匹。

translations.literal: Near the end of Yanxing, King Rian of Goguryeo sought to send a daughter to the inner court; Emperor Xianzu agreed, temporarily appointing Jun Attendant Cavalier at Large, bestowing the title Baron of Anfeng, adding General Who Subdues the Waves, and sending him with staff of authority to Goguryeo to receive the princess, with a gift of a hundred bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Yanxing, King Rian of Goguryeo sought to send a daughter into the inner court; Emperor Xianzu agreed, temporarily appointing Jun Attendant Cavalier at Large, bestowing the title Baron of Anfeng, adding General Who Subdues the Waves, and sending him with staff of authority to Goguryeo to receive the princess, with a gift of a hundred bolts of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 駿至平壤城。

translations.literal: Jun reached Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reached Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 或勸璉曰：「魏昔與燕婚，既而伐之，由行人具其夷險故也。

translations.literal: Someone advised Rian: "Wei once married with Yan, then attacked it — because the envoy had mapped their mountains and passes.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Rian: "Wei once married with Yan, then attacked it — because the envoy had mapped their mountains and passes.

sentences.zh: 今若送女，恐不異於馮氏。」

translations.literal: If you now send a daughter, I fear it will be no different from the Lady Feng affair."
translations.idiomatic: If you now send a daughter, I fear it will be no different from the affair of Lady Feng."

sentences.zh: 璉遂謬言女喪。

translations.literal: Rian then falsely claimed the girl had died.
translations.idiomatic: Rian then falsely claimed the girl had died.

sentences.zh: 駿與璉往復經年，責璉以義方，璉不勝其忿，遂斷駿從者酒食。

translations.literal: Jun and Rian exchanged messages for a year; Jun upbraided Rian on moral principle; Rian, unable to contain his anger, cut off wine and food for Jun's attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Rian exchanged messages for a year; Jun upbraided Rian on moral principle; Rian, unable to contain his anger, cut off wine and food for Jun's attendants.

sentences.zh: 璉欲逼辱之，憚而不敢害。

translations.literal: Rian wished to humiliate him but feared and did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Rian wished to humiliate him but feared to do so and did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 會顯祖崩，乃還，拜祕書令。

translations.literal: When Xianzu died, he returned and was appointed Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu died, he returned and was appointed Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 初遷神主于太廟，有司奏：舊事，廟中執事之官，例皆賜爵，今宜依舊。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablets were first moved to the Grand Temple, the relevant office memorialized: by precedent, officials serving in the temple were routinely ennobled; this should follow the old custom.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablets were first moved to the Grand Temple, the relevant office memorialized: by precedent, officials serving in the temple were routinely ennobled; the old custom should be followed.

sentences.zh: 詔百僚評議，羣臣咸以為宜依舊事，駿獨以為不可。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to discuss; all the ministers held the old custom should be followed; Jun alone disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the hundred officials to discuss; all the ministers held that the old custom should be followed; Jun alone disagreed.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「臣聞：名器為帝王所貴，山河為區夏之重。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I have heard that titles and instruments are what emperors treasure, and mountains and rivers are the weight of the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I have heard that titles and instruments are what emperors treasure, and mountains and rivers are the weight of the central realm.

sentences.zh: 是以漢祖有約，非功不侯。

translations.literal: Therefore Han's Founding Emperor had a covenant: no enfeoffment without merit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Han's Founding Emperor had a covenant: no enfeoffment without merit.

sentences.zh: 必當屬有命於大君之辰，展心力於戰謀之日，然後可以應茅土之錫。

translations.literal: One must have been entrusted with mandate at the great ruler's accession and exerted mind and strength on days of battle and planning — only then may one receive the grant of earth and altar.
translations.idiomatic: One must have been entrusted with mandate at the great ruler's accession and exerted mind and strength on days of battle and planning — only then may one receive the grant of earth and altar.

sentences.zh: 未見預事於宗廟，而獲賞於疆土；

translations.literal: I have never seen one who merely attended affairs in the ancestral temple rewarded with territory;
translations.idiomatic: I have never seen one who merely attended affairs in the ancestral temple rewarded with territory;

sentences.zh: 徒見晉鄭之后以夾輔為至勳，吳鄧之儔以征伐為重績。

translations.literal: I have only seen descendants of Jin and Zheng honored for assisting the throne, and men like Wu and Deng prized for military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I have only seen descendants of Jin and Zheng honored for assisting the throne, and men like Wu and Deng prized for military achievements.

sentences.zh: 周漢既無文於遠代，魏晉亦靡記於往年。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han left no such records in distant ages; Wei and Jin likewise preserved no such precedents in recent years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han left no such records in distant ages; Wei and Jin likewise preserved no such precedents in recent years.

sentences.zh: 自皇道開符，乾業創統，務高三、五之規，思隆百王之軌，罰頗減古，賞實增昔。

translations.literal: Since the imperial way opened its mandate and the heavenly enterprise founded its succession, striving to match the standards of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, thinking to elevate the tracks of the hundred kings — punishments were somewhat lighter than antiquity, rewards more real than before.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial way opened its mandate and the heavenly enterprise founded its succession, striving to match the standards of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and to elevate the tracks of the hundred kings — punishments were somewhat lighter than antiquity, rewards more real than before.

sentences.zh: 時因神主改祔、清廟致肅，而授羣司以九品之命，顯執事以五等之名。

translations.literal: At the time, because the spirit tablets were re-enshrined and the pure temple made solemn, offices were granted nine-rank appointments and functionaries given five-grade titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because the spirit tablets were re-enshrined and the pure temple made solemn, offices were granted nine-rank appointments and functionaries given five-grade titles.

sentences.zh: 雖復帝王制作，弗相沿襲，然當時恩澤，豈足為長世之軌乎？

translations.literal: Though imperial institutions do not simply follow one another, can that moment's grace suffice as a standard for generations?
translations.idiomatic: Though imperial institutions do not simply follow one another, can that moment's grace suffice as a standard for generations?

sentences.zh: 乖眾之愆，伏待罪譴。」

translations.literal: My fault of opposing the multitude — I submit and await punishment."
translations.idiomatic: My fault of opposing the multitude — I submit and await punishment."

sentences.zh: 書奏，從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and accepted.

sentences.zh: 文明太后謂羣臣曰：「言事固當正直而準古典，安可依附暫時舊事乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming told the ministers: "To speak on affairs should indeed be upright and measured against classical models — how can one cling to temporary old precedents?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming told the ministers: "To speak on affairs should indeed be upright and measured against classical models — how can one cling to temporary old precedents?"

sentences.zh: 賜駿衣一襲、帛二百匹。

translations.literal: She bestowed on Jun one suit of clothes and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: She bestowed on Jun one suit of clothes and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 駿又表曰：「春秋有云：見有禮於其君者，若孝子之養父母；

translations.literal: Jun again memorialized: "The Spring and Autumn Annals says: seeing one who shows courtesy to his ruler is like a filial son nourishing his parents;
translations.idiomatic: Jun again memorialized: "The Spring and Autumn Annals says: seeing one who shows courtesy to his ruler is like a filial son nourishing his parents;

sentences.zh: 見無禮於其君者，若鷹鸇之逐鳥雀。

translations.literal: seeing one who shows discourtesy to his ruler is like a hawk pursuing sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: seeing one who shows discourtesy to his ruler is like a hawk pursuing sparrows.

sentences.zh: 所以勸誡將來，垂範萬代。

translations.literal: This is to admonish the future and leave a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: This is to admonish the future and leave a model for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 昔陳恒殺君，宣尼請討，雖欲晏逸，其得已乎？

translations.literal: Formerly when Chen Heng killed his ruler, Confucius asked for punitive action — though he wished to rest at ease, could he have desisted?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Chen Heng killed his ruler, Confucius asked for punitive action — though he wished to rest at ease, could he have desisted?

sentences.zh: 今廟算天回，七州雲動，將水蕩鯨鯢，陸掃凶逆。

translations.literal: Now the temple calculations turn with heaven; seven provinces stir like clouds; on the water we shall wash away whales and sea monsters, on land sweep away the violent rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven itself favors our plans in the temple; seven provinces rise like storm clouds; on the rivers we shall wash away the great rebels, on land sweep away the violent enemy.

sentences.zh: 然戰貴不陳，兵家所美。

translations.literal: Yet warfare prizes avoiding pitched battle — this the strategists praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet warfare prizes avoiding pitched battle — this the strategists praise.

sentences.zh: 宜先遣劉昶招喻淮南。

translations.literal: We should first send Liu Chang to summon and persuade Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: We should first send Liu Chang to summon and persuade Huainan.

sentences.zh: 若應聲響悅，同心齊舉，則長江之險，可朝服而濟，道成之首，可崇朝而懸。

translations.literal: If they respond gladly in echo and rise together in unity, the Yangzi's barrier could be crossed in court robes by morning; Xiao Daocheng's head could be hung by noon.
translations.idiomatic: If they respond gladly in echo and rise together in unity, the Yangzi's barrier could be crossed in court robes by morning; Xiao Daocheng's head could be hung by noon.

sentences.zh: 苟江南之輕薄，背劉氏之恩義，則曲在彼矣，何負神明哉！

translations.literal: If the frivolous south betrays the Liu family's grace and righteousness, the fault lies with them — why would we owe Heaven anything?
translations.idiomatic: If the frivolous south betrays the Liu family's grace and righteousness, the fault lies with them — why would we owe Heaven anything?

sentences.zh: 直義檄江南，振旅回斾，亦足以示救患之大仁，揚義風於四海。

translations.literal: To issue a proclamation of upright righteousness to Jiangnan, rally the army and turn the banners homeward, would also suffice to display the great benevolence of relieving distress and spread the righteous wind across the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Even a righteous proclamation to Jiangnan, followed by rallying the army and turning home, would show enough benevolence in relieving distress and spread our righteous repute across the realm.

sentences.zh: 且攻難守易，則力懸百倍，不可不深思，不可不熟慮。

translations.literal: Moreover, attack is hard while defense is easy — thus the disparity in strength is a hundredfold; this cannot but be deeply pondered, cannot but be thoroughly considered.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, attack is hard and defense easy, so the disparity in strength may run a hundredfold — this demands deep thought and careful deliberation.

sentences.zh: 今天下雖謐，方外猶虞，拾夤僥倖於西南，狂虜伺舋於漠北。

translations.literal: Now though the realm is tranquil, beyond the borders there is still cause for concern — Shiyin seeks opportunistic advantage in the southwest, while wild barbarians watch for openings in the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is at peace, the frontiers still give cause for worry — Shiyin of Tuyuhun seeks advantage in the southwest, while fierce enemies on the northern steppe watch for their chance.

sentences.zh: 脫攻不稱心，恐兵不卒解，兵不卒解，則憂慮逾深。

translations.literal: If the attack should fail to satisfy expectations, I fear the army will not soon be disbanded; if the army is not soon disbanded, then anxieties deepen ever further.
translations.idiomatic: If the campaign falls short of expectations, the army may not be withdrawn quickly; and if the army cannot be withdrawn quickly, our worries will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 夫為社稷之計者，莫不先於守本。

translations.literal: Those who plan for the altars of state never fail to put guarding the foundation first.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone planning for the state's welfare must put securing the foundation first.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為觀兵江滸，振曜皇威，宜特加撫慰。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that displaying troops on the river shore and flashing imperial majesty should especially include added reassurance and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully suggest that in displaying troops on the Yangzi's banks and projecting imperial majesty, special care should be taken to reassure and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 秋毫無犯，則民知德信；

translations.literal: If not even the slightest thing is violated, then the people will know virtue and trust;
translations.idiomatic: If not even the slightest harm is done, the people will know our virtue and good faith;

sentences.zh: 民知德信，則襁負而來；

translations.literal: when the people know virtue and trust, they will come carrying their infants on their backs;
translations.idiomatic: when they know our virtue and good faith, they will come bringing even their infants on their backs;

sentences.zh: 襁負而來，則淮北可定；

translations.literal: when they come carrying infants on their backs, north of the Huai can be settled;
translations.idiomatic: once they come flocking in, north of the Huai can be secured;

sentences.zh: 淮北可定，則吳寇異圖；

translations.literal: when north of the Huai is settled, the Wu invaders will shift their designs;
translations.idiomatic: once north of the Huai is secured, the Wu enemy will change their plans;

sentences.zh: 寇圖異則禍釁出。

translations.literal: when the invaders' designs shift, disaster and strife will emerge.
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy changes their plans, disaster and strife will break out among them.

sentences.zh: 然後觀釁而動，則不晚矣。

translations.literal: Only then watch for the opening and move — and it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Only then, watching for the opening to strike, we would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 請停諸州之兵，且待後舉。

translations.literal: I beg that the armies of the various provinces be halted and a later campaign await.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the armies of the provinces be halted pending a later campaign.

sentences.zh: 所謂守本者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called guarding the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by securing the foundation.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下、太皇太后英算神規，彌綸百勝之外；

translations.literal: Humbly reflecting, Your Majesty and the Grand Empress Dowager possess brilliant stratagems and divine plans that extend beyond a hundred victories;
translations.idiomatic: Humbly reflecting, Your Majesty and the Grand Empress Dowager possess brilliant stratagems and divine wisdom extending beyond mere battlefield triumph;

sentences.zh: 應機體變，獨悟方寸之中。

translations.literal: adapting to circumstances and grasping change, you alone comprehend it within your breast.
translations.idiomatic: adapting to circumstances and grasping change with insight known only in your own heart.

sentences.zh: 臣影頹虞淵，昏耄將及，雖思憂國，終無云補。」

translations.literal: Your servant's shadow fades at the abyss of Yu — senility is near; though I think on serving the state, in the end I can offer no aid."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's shadow fades like the sun at Yu-yuan — old age is upon me; though my heart is full of concern for the state, I can offer nothing of use."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: His advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 沙門法秀謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: The monk Faxiu plotted rebellion and was executed upon discovery.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Faxiu plotted rebellion and was executed when his plot was uncovered.

sentences.zh: 駿表曰：「臣聞詩之作也，蓋以言志。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized: "Your servant has heard that the making of the Odes is essentially to give voice to one's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized: "Your servant has heard that the Odes were composed essentially to give voice to one's intent.

sentences.zh: 邇之事父，遠之事君，關諸風俗，靡不備焉。

translations.literal: In the near, they serve the father; in the far, they serve the ruler — touching on customs, nothing is lacking therein.
translations.idiomatic: Near at hand they guide filial duty to fathers; at a distance they guide loyal service to rulers — touching on every custom, nothing is left out.

sentences.zh: 上可以頌美聖德，下可以申厚風化，言之者無罪，聞之者足以誡。

translations.literal: Above they can praise holy virtue; below they can extend thickening transformation — those who speak them are without guilt, those who hear them are sufficient to take warning.
translations.idiomatic: Above they can praise sage virtue; below they can promote moral transformation — those who speak them incur no blame, and those who hear them receive adequate admonition.

sentences.zh: 此古人用詩之本意。

translations.literal: This is the ancient purpose in using the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ancients' original purpose in using poetry.

sentences.zh: 臣以垂沒之年，得逢盛明之運，雖復昏耄將及，猶慕廉頗強飯之風。

translations.literal: Your servant, in the years of declining life, has encountered an age of flourishing brilliance; though senility is again near, I still admire the spirit of Lian Po, who ate heartily in old age.
translations.idiomatic: In my declining years I have been fortunate enough to live in this flourishing age; though old age is upon me, I still aspire to the spirit of Lian Po, who kept his vigor to the end.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下、太皇太后，道合天地，明侔日月，則天與唐風斯穆，順帝與周道通靈。

translations.literal: Humbly reflecting, Your Majesty and the Grand Empress Dowager — your Way aligns with Heaven and Earth, your brilliance equals sun and moon: conforming to Heaven, you share in the gravitas of Tang feng; following the Emperor's course, you commune with the numinous way of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly reflecting, Your Majesty and the Grand Empress Dowager — your Way accords with Heaven and Earth, your brilliance equals sun and moon: as Heaven's chosen, you match the solemn virtue of Tang; as rightful sovereigns, you share in the numinous Way of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 是以狂妖懷逆，無隱謀之地；

translations.literal: Thus when mad demons harbor rebellion, there is no place to hide their plots;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when mad rebels harbor treachery, they have nowhere to hide their plots;

sentences.zh: 冥靈潛翦，伏發覺之誅。

translations.literal: dark spirits secretly cut them down, and they are executed upon discovery of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: unseen spirits cut them down in secret, and they face execution the moment their plot is discovered.

sentences.zh: 用能七廟幽贊，人神扶助者已。

translations.literal: By this the seven temples receive hidden support, and men and spirits lend aid.
translations.idiomatic: By this the ancestral temples receive unseen endorsement, and both men and spirits lend their support.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝喜踴。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot contain his overflowing joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is overcome with joy.

sentences.zh: 謹竭老鈍之思，上慶國頌十六章，并序巡狩、甘雨之德焉。」

translations.literal: I respectfully exhaust my aged and dull mind, submitting sixteen stanzas celebrating the state, together with prefaces to the virtues of the imperial tour and sweet rain."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully offer these verses from my aging mind — sixteen stanzas celebrating the state, with introductions to the virtues shown in the imperial tour and the sweet rain."

sentences.zh: 其頌曰：

translations.literal: The eulogy says:
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads:

sentences.zh: 乾德不言，四時迭序。

translations.literal: Heaven's virtue speaks not, yet the four seasons pass in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's virtue is silent, yet the four seasons follow in turn.

sentences.zh: 於皇大魏，則天承祜。

translations.literal: O august Great Wei — conforming to Heaven, receiving blessing.
translations.idiomatic: O resplendent Great Wei — Heaven's chosen, blessed from above.

sentences.zh: 疊聖三宗，重明四祖。

translations.literal: Sage upon sage for three generations, doubly luminous for four ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Sage succeeds sage through three reigns, doubly luminous through four founders.

sentences.zh: 豈伊殷周，遐契三、五。

translations.literal: How could it be only Yin and Zhou — afar they align with the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Not merely the Yin and Zhou — they reach back to match the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 明明在上，聖敬日新。

translations.literal: Brightly bright on high, sage reverence renews daily.
translations.idiomatic: Radiantly enthroned on high, sage reverence grows day by day.

sentences.zh: 汪汪叡后，體治垂仁。

translations.literal: Vast and vast the wise sovereign, embodying good governance and extending benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Vast in wisdom, the sage ruler embodies good governance and extends benevolence to all.

sentences.zh: 德從風穆，教與化津。

translations.literal: Virtue follows like wind's gentleness; teaching joins transformation as a ford.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue spreads gently as the wind; instruction joins transformation like a ford across the waters.

sentences.zh: 千載昌運，道隆茲辰。

translations.literal: A thousand-year era of prosperous fortune — the Way is exalted in this moment.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand-year age of prosperity — the Way reaches its height in this hour.

sentences.zh: 歲惟巡狩，應運遊田。

translations.literal: This year the imperial tour; responding to Heaven's mandate, roaming the fields.
translations.idiomatic: This year the sovereign tours the realm, hunting in the fields as Heaven ordains.

sentences.zh: 省方問苦，訪政高年。

translations.literal: Inspecting the regions, inquiring into hardship; visiting governance among the elderly.
translations.idiomatic: He inspects the provinces and inquires into suffering; he seeks the counsel of the aged on governance.

sentences.zh: 咸秩百靈，柴望山川。

translations.literal: All ranks the hundred spirits; faggot-burning and gazing toward mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He properly ranks the hundred spirits; he burns offerings and gazes toward the mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 誰云禮滯，遇聖則宣。

translations.literal: Who says rites are stagnant? Encountering a sage, they are proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Who would say rites have fallen into disuse? Under a sage, they flourish anew.

sentences.zh: 王業初定，中山是由。

translations.literal: The royal enterprise newly established — through Zhongshan it was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial enterprise was first established, Zhongshan was the path taken.

sentences.zh: 臨幸之盛，情特綢繆。

translations.literal: The grandeur of the imperial visit — feeling especially tender and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The grandeur of the imperial visit shows special tenderness and care.

sentences.zh: 仰歌祖業，俯欣春柔。

translations.literal: Looking up, singing the ancestors' enterprise; looking down, rejoicing in spring's gentleness.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up, he sings the ancestors' achievement; looking down, he delights in the gentle spring.

sentences.zh: 大哉肆眚，蕩民百憂。

translations.literal: Great is the general amnesty — washing away the people's hundred woes.
translations.idiomatic: Great is the general amnesty — it washes away the people's every care.

sentences.zh: 百憂既蕩，與之更初。

translations.literal: Once the hundred woes are washed away, with them comes a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Once every care is washed away, the people begin anew.

sentences.zh: 邕邕億兆，戶詠來蘇。

translations.literal: Harmoniously, harmoniously, a hundred million — every household chants of returning renewal.
translations.idiomatic: In harmony, countless multitudes — every household sings of renewal and relief.

sentences.zh: 忽有狂竪，謀逆聖都。

translations.literal: Suddenly there arose a mad upstart plotting rebellion against the sacred capital.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a mad rebel plotted treason against the sacred capital.

sentences.zh: 明靈幽告，發覺伏誅。

translations.literal: Bright spirits secretly revealed it; discovered upon the plot, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bright spirits gave secret warning; the plot was discovered and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 羿浞為亂，祖龍千紀。

translations.literal: Yi and Zhuo brought chaos; the First Emperor's thousand-year reign.
translations.idiomatic: Chaos came with Yi and Han Zhuo; the First Emperor's thousand-year destiny.

sentences.zh: 狂華冬茂，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Wild flowers bloom in winter — it has ever been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Madness flowering in winter — this has always happened.

sentences.zh: 美哉皇度，道固千祀。

translations.literal: How beautiful the imperial measure — the Way is firm for a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: How beautiful the imperial measure — the Way endures for a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 百靈潛翦，姦不遑起。

translations.literal: The hundred spirits secretly cut them down — treachery has no chance to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred spirits cut them down in secret — treachery never gets the chance to rise.

sentences.zh: 姦不遑起，罪人得情。

translations.literal: Treachery having no chance to rise, the guilty receive fitting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When treachery cannot rise, the guilty receive what they deserve.

sentences.zh: 憲章刑律，五秩猶輕。

translations.literal: The statutes of law and punishment — even the five punishments are still lenient.
translations.idiomatic: By the statutes of penal law, even the five punishments seem lenient.

sentences.zh: 於穆二聖，仁等春生。

translations.literal: So solemn, the two sages — benevolence equal to spring's birth.
translations.idiomatic: So solemn are the two sages — their benevolence equals the renewing force of spring.

sentences.zh: 除棄周漢，遐軌犧庭。

translations.literal: Setting aside Zhou and Han, far tracking the court of Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Zhou and Han behind, they follow the distant model of Fuxi's court.

sentences.zh: 周漢奚棄？

translations.literal: Why set aside Zhou and Han?
translations.idiomatic: Why leave Zhou and Han behind?

sentences.zh: 忿彼苛刻。

translations.literal: Resenting their harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: Because of their harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 犧庭曷軌？

translations.literal: Why track Fuxi's court?
translations.idiomatic: Why follow Fuxi's court?

sentences.zh: 希仁尚德。

translations.literal: Aspiring to benevolence, honoring virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because they aspire to benevolence and honor virtue.

sentences.zh: 徽音一振，聲教四塞。

translations.literal: One flourish of splendid tone — moral teaching fills the four borders.
translations.idiomatic: One flourish of their noble voice — civilizing instruction fills the four corners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 豈惟京甸，化播萬國。

translations.literal: Not only the capital district — transformation spreads to ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Not only the capital region — their transforming influence reaches every land.

sentences.zh: 誠信幽贊，陰陽以調。

translations.literal: Sincerity and trust receive hidden endorsement — yin and yang thus harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity and trust win unseen blessing — yin and yang fall into harmony.

sentences.zh: 谷風扇夕，甘雨降朝。

translations.literal: Valley wind fans at evening; sweet rain falls at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The valley breeze blows at evening; sweet rain falls at dawn.

sentences.zh: 嘉生含穎，深盛熙苗。

translations.literal: Fine crops hold their tips; deep and flourishing, the verdant seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: Fine crops show their budding tips; deep and flourishing grow the verdant seedlings.

sentences.zh: 鰥貧巷詠，寡婦室謠。

translations.literal: Widowers and the poor chant in the lanes; widows sing in their chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers and the poor sing in the lanes; widows chant in their homes.

sentences.zh: 聞諸詩者，雲漢賦宣。

translations.literal: Those who hear these Odes say: the "Clouded Heavens" ode proclaims it.
translations.idiomatic: Those versed in the Odes say it is proclaimed in the "Clouded Heavens."

sentences.zh: 章句迥秀，英昭雅篇。

translations.literal: Its lines and clauses uniquely splendid — its brilliance illumines the elegant canon.
translations.idiomatic: Its verses stand uniquely splendid — its brilliance illumines the great elegancies of the canon.

sentences.zh: 矧乃盛明，德隆道玄。

translations.literal: How much more in this flourishing brilliance — virtue is exalted, the Way is profound.
translations.idiomatic: How much more in this resplendent age — virtue is exalted and the Way profound.

sentences.zh: 豈唯兩施，神徵豐年。

translations.literal: Not only the paired grants — divine signs mark a bountiful year.
translations.idiomatic: Not only the double bounty of rain — divine signs herald a harvest year.

sentences.zh: 豐年盛矣，化無不濃。

translations.literal: The bountiful year is abundant — transformation nowhere is not rich.
translations.idiomatic: The harvest year is rich indeed — transformation nowhere fails to reach.

sentences.zh: 有禮有樂，政莫不通。

translations.literal: With rites and with music — in governance nothing fails to penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: With rites and music, no aspect of governance fails to thrive.

sentences.zh: 咨臣延躍，欣詠時邕。

translations.literal: Your minister leaps forward with joy, delighting to chant the harmonious season.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister leaps with joy, delighting to sing of this harmonious age.

sentences.zh: 誰云易遇，曠齡一逢。

translations.literal: Who says such an encounter is easy? Once in an empty lifetime one meets it.
translations.idiomatic: Who would say such an age is easily met? Once in a lifetime one may encounter it.

sentences.zh: 上天無親，唯德是在。

translations.literal: High Heaven is without partiality — only virtue is what it attends to.
translations.idiomatic: High Heaven shows no partiality — only virtue draws its favor.

sentences.zh: 思樂盛明，雖疲勿怠。

translations.literal: Reflecting joy on this flourishing brilliance — though weary, do not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Rejoice in this resplendent age — though wearied, do not slacken.

sentences.zh: 差之毫釐，千里之倍。

translations.literal: Missing by a hair's breadth — a thousand li's error.
translations.idiomatic: A miss of a hair's breadth can become an error of a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 願言勞謙，求仁不悔。

translations.literal: I wish to speak of toiling humility — seeking benevolence without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I pray for humble diligence — seeking benevolence without regret.

sentences.zh: 人亦有言，聖主慎微。

translations.literal: Men also have a saying: the sage ruler is careful of the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: As men say, the sage ruler is careful of the smallest things.

sentences.zh: 五國連兵，踰年歷時。

translations.literal: Five kingdoms joined in arms — spanning years and seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Five kingdoms joined in war — year after year, season after season.

sentences.zh: 鹿車而運，廟算失思。

translations.literal: Carts like deer in flight for transport — temple calculations lose their wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Convoys stream like fleeing deer — strategic planning loses its way.

sentences.zh: 有司不惠。

translations.literal: The responsible officials show no kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials show no mercy.

sentences.zh: 蠶食役煩。

translations.literal: Nibbling away like silkworms — corvée labor becomes burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Demands eat away like silkworms — corvée labor grows unbearable.

sentences.zh: 民不堪命，將家逃山。

translations.literal: The people cannot bear their orders — leading their families they flee to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot bear their plight — families flee to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 宜督厥守，威德是宣。

translations.literal: One should supervise those guardians — majesty and virtue are what must be proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Those in charge should be overseen — majesty and virtue must be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 威德如何？

translations.literal: What are majesty and virtue like?
translations.idiomatic: What should majesty and virtue look like?

sentences.zh: 聚眾盈川。

translations.literal: Gathering the multitude to fill the rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering the masses until rivers brim with people.

sentences.zh: 民之從令，實賴衣食。

translations.literal: The people's following of commands truly depends on food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The people's obedience truly depends on food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 農桑失本，誰耕誰織？

translations.literal: Agriculture and sericulture lose their foundation — who will plow, who will weave?
translations.idiomatic: When farming and sericulture lose their foundation — who will plow, who will weave?

sentences.zh: 飢寒切身，易子而食。

translations.literal: Hunger and cold touch the body — they exchange children to eat.
translations.idiomatic: With hunger and cold at their door — they exchange children to eat.

sentences.zh: 靜言念之，實懷歎息。

translations.literal: Calmly speaking, reflecting on this — truly my heart holds sighs.
translations.idiomatic: When I reflect quietly on this, my heart can only sigh.

sentences.zh: 昔聞典論，非位不謀。

translations.literal: Formerly I heard in canonical discourse: not in office, do not plan.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the canonical teaching: outside one's office, do not meddle in policy.

sentences.zh: 漆室憂國，遺芳載臭。

translations.literal: The Lady of Lacquer Chamber worried for the state — her fragrance and foulness alike are recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Lacquer Chamber worried for the state — her fame lives on, for good or ill.

sentences.zh: 咨臣昏老，偏蒙恩祐。

translations.literal: Your minister, dim and old, has specially received grace and protection.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble minister, old and dim of sight, has been specially favored with grace.

sentences.zh: 忽忘狂瞽，敢獻愚陋。

translations.literal: Suddenly forgetting my mad blindness, I dare offer this foolish crudity.
translations.idiomatic: Forgetting my reckless blindness, I dare offer this humble counsel.

sentences.zh: 文明太后令曰：「省詩表，聞之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "I have reviewed the poetry memorial and heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "I have reviewed your poetry memorial and received it.

sentences.zh: 歌頌宗祖之功德可爾，當世之言，何其過也。

translations.literal: To sing and praise the ancestors' achievements and virtue is acceptable; as for words about the present age — how excessive they are!
translations.idiomatic: Praise of the ancestors' achievements is fitting enough, but your words about the present age go too far.

sentences.zh: 所箴下章，戢之不忘。」

translations.literal: As for the admonitions in the sections below, keep them and do not forget."
translations.idiomatic: Your admonitions in the sections below — I will keep them and not forget.

sentences.zh: 駿又奏得一頌，始於固業，終於無為，十篇。

translations.literal: Jun also submitted an eulogy, beginning with Solid Foundation and ending with Non-Action, ten pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also submitted an eulogy cycle of ten pieces, opening with "Solid Foundation" and closing with "Non-Action."

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: Most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 文明太后令曰：「省表并頌十篇，聞之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "I have reviewed the memorial and the ten eulogies and heard them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming issued an order: "I have reviewed your memorial and the ten eulogies and received them.

sentences.zh: 鑒戒既備，良用欽玩。

translations.literal: Mirrors and warnings are complete; I greatly esteem and enjoy them.
translations.idiomatic: Your mirrors and warnings are complete — I greatly esteem and delight in them.

sentences.zh: 養老乞言，其斯之謂。」
