translations.literal: Honoring the aged and soliciting counsel — this is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by honoring the aged and soliciting counsel.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「程駿歷官清慎，言事每愜。

translations.literal: An edict also said: "Cheng Jun served in office with purity and caution; in presenting affairs he was always satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said: "Cheng Jun served in office with purity and discretion, and his memorials were always to the point.

sentences.zh: 又門無俠貨之賓，室有懷道之士。

translations.literal: Moreover, his gate had no guests bearing flashy goods; his house had men cherishing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: His gate admitted no guests bearing flashy gifts, yet his house held men devoted to the Way.

sentences.zh: 可賜帛六百匹，旌其儉德。」

translations.literal: He may be granted six hundred bolts of silk to honor his frugal virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him six hundred bolts of silk to honor his frugal virtue.

sentences.zh: 駿悉散之親舊。

translations.literal: Jun distributed it all to relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jun distributed the entire gift among relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 性介直，不競時榮。

translations.literal: By nature upright and direct, he did not compete for temporal glory.
translations.idiomatic: By nature upright and direct, he did not compete for worldly advancement.

sentences.zh: 太和九年正月，病篤，乃遺令曰：「吾存尚儉薄，豈可沒為奢厚哉？

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Taihe, his illness was grave, and he left testamentary instructions: "In life I still value thrift and simplicity — how could I in death be lavish and thick?
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of the Taihe era, his illness grew grave, and he left testamentary instructions: "In life I still valued thrift and simplicity — how could I in death be buried in luxury?

sentences.zh: 昔王孫裸葬，有感而然；

translations.literal: In antiquity Wang Sun had a bare burial — moved, one proceeds thus;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Wang Sun was buried naked, moved by principle to do so;

sentences.zh: 士安籧篨，頗亦矯厲。

translations.literal: Shi An used bamboo mat and coarse cloth — also rather extreme corrective.
translations.idiomatic: Shi An chose a bamboo mat and coarse cloth — also rather an extreme corrective.

sentences.zh: 今世既休明，百度循禮，彼非吾志也。

translations.literal: The present age is already enlightened and brilliant; all affairs follow ritual — those are not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The present age is already enlightened and all affairs follow ritual — those examples are not my intent.

sentences.zh: 可斂以時服，器皿從古。」

translations.literal: Wrap me in the clothes of the season; utensils according to ancient custom."
translations.idiomatic: Wrap me in seasonal dress and use utensils according to ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 遂卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He then died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 初，駿病甚，高祖、文明太后遣使者更問其疾，敕御師徐謇診視，[9]賜以湯藥。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jun's illness was severe, Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming sent emissaries repeatedly to inquire after his illness, ordered Imperial Physician Xu Qian to examine him, [9] and granted him decoctions and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jun's illness was severe, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent emissaries repeatedly to inquire after him, ordered Imperial Physician Xu Qian to examine him, [9] and granted him decoctions and medicines.

sentences.zh: 臨終，詔以小子公稱為中散，從子靈虬為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At his deathbed, an edict appointed his youngest son Gongcheng as Palace Attendant and his nephew Lingqiu as Assistant Compilation Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed, an edict appointed his youngest son Gongcheng as Palace Attendant and his nephew Lingqiu as Assistant Compilation Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及卒，高祖、文明太后傷惜之，賜東園祕器、朝服一稱、帛三百匹，贈冠軍將軍、兗州刺史、曲安侯，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming grieved for him, granted Eastern Garden funerary regalia, one set of court dress, three hundred bolts of silk, posthumously awarded Champion General, Inspector of Yanzhou, Marquis of Qu'an, posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming mourned him deeply, granted Eastern Garden funerary regalia, one set of court dress, and three hundred bolts of silk, and posthumously honored him as Champion General, inspector of Yanzhou, and Marquis of Qu'an, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 所製文筆，自有集錄。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were collected in a separate compilation.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions were collected in a separate compilation.

sentences.zh: 駿六子，元繼、公達、公亮、公禮，並無官。

translations.literal: Jun had six sons: Yuanji, Gongda, Gongliang, and Gongli — all without office.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had six sons; Yuanji, Gongda, Gongliang, and Gongli all held no office.

sentences.zh: 公義，侍御史、謁者僕射、都水使者、武昌王司馬、沛郡太守。

translations.literal: Gongyi: Attending Censor, Director of the Masters of Ceremonials, Commissioner of Waterworks, Military Administrator for the Prince of Wuchang, Administrator of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi served as Attending Censor, Director of the Masters of Ceremonials, Commissioner of Waterworks, military administrator for the Prince of Wuchang, and administrator of Pei.

sentences.zh: 公稱，主文中散、給事中、尚書郎。

translations.literal: Gongcheng: Chief Textual Palace Attendant, Palace Attendant Within the Gates, Master of Writing Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Gongcheng served as Chief Textual Palace Attendant, Palace Attendant Within the Gates, and Master of Writing Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 並早卒。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: Both died young.

sentences.zh: 公禮子畿，字世伯。

translations.literal: Gongli's son Ji, style Shibo.
translations.idiomatic: Gongli's son was Ji, whose style was Shibo.

sentences.zh: 好學，頗有文才。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, with considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 荊州府主簿。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Jingzhou prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of the Jingzhou prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 始駿從祖弟伯達，伯達名犯顯祖廟諱。

translations.literal: Originally Jun's younger cousin from the great-grandfather's line, Boda — Boda's name violated the temple taboo of Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger cousin from the great-grandfather's line was Boda, whose given name violated the temple taboo of Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 與駿同年，亦以文辯。

translations.literal: Same age as Jun, also known for literary eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: He was the same age as Jun and was also known for literary eloquence.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna in the text.〉

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍時，俱選與牧犍世子參乘出入，時論美之。

translations.literal: During Juqu Mujian's time, both were selected to attend the heir as carriage companions going in and out; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: During Juqu Mujian's reign, both were chosen to attend the heir as carriage companions in and out of court, and contemporary opinion praised them.

sentences.zh: 伯達早亡。

translations.literal: Boda died young.
translations.idiomatic: Boda died young.

sentences.zh: 弟子靈虬幼孤，頗有文才，而久淪末役。

translations.literal: Jun's nephew Lingqiu was orphaned young, had considerable literary talent, yet long sank into lowly service.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's nephew Lingqiu was orphaned young and had considerable literary talent, yet for long he languished in lowly clerical posts.

sentences.zh: 在吏職十餘年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In clerical office for more than ten years, dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He served in clerical posts for more than ten years before being dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 會駿臨終啟請，得擢為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Jun on his deathbed submitted a petition, he was promoted to Assistant Compilation Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun submitted a petition on his deathbed, Lingqiu was promoted to Assistant Compilation Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後坐稱在京無緦親，而高祖知其與駿子公義為始族，故致譴免。

translations.literal: Later, convicted for claiming to have no close kin in the capital — but Emperor Gaozu knew he and Jun's son Gongyi were of the same founding clan, and so had him censured and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was convicted for claiming to have no close kin in the capital, but Emperor Xiaowen knew that he and Jun's son Gongyi were of the same founding clan, and so had him censured and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 至洛，無官，貧病。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, he had no office and was poor and ill.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang he held no office and was poor and ill.

sentences.zh: 久之，崔光啟申為羽林監，選補徐州、梁郡太守，以酗酒為刺史武昌王鑒所劾，失官。

translations.literal: After a long time, Cui Guang petitioned to have him appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest; selected and assigned as Administrator of Liang commandery in Xuzhou — indicted for drunkenness by Inspector Prince of Wuchang Jian, and lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, Cui Guang petitioned to have him appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest; he was then selected and appointed administrator of Liang commandery in Xuzhou, but was indicted for drunkenness by the inspector, Prince of Wuchang Jian, and lost his office.

sentences.zh: 既下梁郡，志力少衰，猶時為酒困。

translations.literal: Once he went down to Liang commandery, his will and strength declined somewhat, yet he was still sometimes beset by wine.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up his post in Liang commandery, his resolve and strength declined somewhat, yet he was still sometimes overcome by wine.

sentences.zh: 久去官祿，不免飢寒，屢詣尚書乞効舊任。

translations.literal: Long away from official salary, he could not escape hunger and cold; repeatedly he went to the Masters of Writing begging to serve in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Long deprived of official salary, he could not escape hunger and cold and repeatedly went to the Masters of Writing begging to serve again in his former capacity.

sentences.zh: 僕射高肇領選，還申為著作郎，以崔光領任，敕令外敍。

translations.literal: Vice Director Gao Zhao oversaw selection and again had him appointed Compilation Gentleman; with Cui Guang holding the concurrent post, an edict ordered external appointment notation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Gao Zhao, overseeing selection, again had him appointed Compilation Gentleman; with Cui Guang holding the concurrent post, an edict ordered his appointment recorded externally.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韓麒麟以才器識用，遂見紀於齊土。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Han Qilin, through talent, capacity, and discernment in employment, came to be recorded in Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Han Qilin, through talent, capacity, and discernment in employment, came to be recorded in Qi territory.

sentences.zh: 顯宗文學立己，屢陳時務，至於實錄之功，所未聞也。

translations.literal: Xianzong established himself through literary learning, repeatedly presenting affairs of the age — as for achievement in truthful recording, none has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong established himself through literary learning and repeatedly presented affairs of the age, but as for achievement in truthful recording, none has been heard.

sentences.zh: 子熙清尚自守，榮過其器。

translations.literal: Zixi was pure and high-minded in self-restraint; glory exceeded his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zixi was pure and high-minded in self-restraint, yet the honors he received exceeded his capacity.

sentences.zh: 程駿才業未多，見知於世者，蓋當時之長策乎？

translations.literal: Cheng Jun's talent and achievement were not abundant — what the world recognized in him was perhaps the long-range policies of the age?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jun's talent and achievement were not great — was what the world recognized in him perhaps the far-reaching policies of his age?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 拷掠胡定 諸本「掠」字缺，冊府卷七一五

translations.literal: [On the passage] "beat and plunder Hu Ding": in all editions the character 掠 is missing; Cefu yuangui, juan 715
translations.idiomatic: [Passage "beat and plunder Hu Ding"] In all editions the character 掠 is absent; Cefu yuangui, juan 715

sentences.zh: 〈八五０二頁〉
作「掠拷」，今據補「掠」字。

translations.literal: has "掠拷"; the character 掠 is now supplied on that evidence.
translations.idiomatic: reads 掠拷; the character 掠 is now supplied on that evidence.

sentences.zh: 唯諮是從 冊府同上卷頁「諮」作「諾」。

translations.literal: [On the phrase] "唯諮是從": in Cefu, same juan and page, 諮 is written as 諾.
translations.idiomatic: [Phrase "唯諮是從"] In Cefu, same juan and page, 諮 appears as 諾.

sentences.zh: 按「唯諮是從」語意晦澀，「諮」當是「諾」之訛。

translations.literal: Comment: The phrase "唯諮是從" is obscure in meaning; 諮 must be a corruption of 諾.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: The phrase "唯諮是從" is obscure in meaning; 諮 must be a corruption of 諾.

sentences.zh: 為國巨患 諸本「巨」作「臣」，獨局本作「巨」。

translations.literal: [On the phrase] "為國巨患": in all editions 巨 is written as 臣; only the Ju ben has 巨.
translations.idiomatic: [Phrase "為國巨患"] In all editions 巨 appears as 臣; only the Ju ben has 巨.

sentences.zh: 按作「臣」不可通，冊府

translations.literal: Comment: Read as 臣 it makes no sense; Cefu yuangui
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Read as 臣 the phrase makes no sense; Cefu yuangui

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same juan and page〉

sentences.zh: 也作「巨」，今從局本。

translations.literal: also has 巨; we now follow the Ju ben.
translations.idiomatic: also has 巨; the text now follows the Ju ben.

sentences.zh: 雖賑貸普霑今猶恐來夏菜色 諸本無「貸」字，語氣不完，今據冊府卷四七二

translations.literal: [On the passage] "雖賑貸普霑今猶恐來夏菜色": in all editions 貸 is absent and the sense is incomplete; now supplemented from Cefu yuangui, juan 472
translations.idiomatic: [Passage "雖賑貸普霑今猶恐來夏菜色"] All editions lack 貸 and the sense is incomplete; it is now supplied from Cefu yuangui, juan 472

sentences.zh: 〈五六二五頁〉
補。

translations.literal: Supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Supplied.

sentences.zh: 又冊府「恐」作「愍雨」二字，兩通，今不改。

translations.literal: Moreover, in Cefu 恐 is written as the two characters 愍雨; both readings are acceptable; we make no change.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in Cefu 恐 appears as the two characters 愍雨; both readings are acceptable, and no change is made.

sentences.zh: 未多坐盜棄市 諸本「多」上無「未」字，北史卷四０韓麒麟附韓顯宗傳、冊府卷四七二

translations.literal: [On the passage] "未多坐盜棄市": in all editions there is no 未 above 多; Beishi, juan 40, Han Qilin appended biography of Han Xianzong; Cefu yuangui, juan 472
translations.idiomatic: [Passage "未多坐盜棄市"] All editions lack 未 before 多; Beishi, juan 40, appended biography of Han Xianzong under Han Qilin; Cefu yuangui, juan 472

sentences.zh: 〈五六二六頁〉
有。

translations.literal: have it.
translations.idiomatic: have it.

sentences.zh: 按顯宗意謂嚴刑無效，若無「未」字，便和原意相反，今據補。

translations.literal: Comment: Xianzong's meaning is that harsh punishments were ineffective; without 未 the sense would be reversed; we now supply it on that evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Xianzong means that harsh punishments were ineffective; without 未 the sense would be reversed, and it is now supplied on that evidence.

sentences.zh: 至於開伎作宦途 諸本「於」訛「與」，今據北史卷四０、冊府卷四七二

translations.literal: [On the passage] "至於開伎作宦途": in all editions 於 is corrupted as 與; now corrected on the authority of Beishi, juan 40, and Cefu yuangui, juan 472
translations.idiomatic: [Passage "至於開伎作宦途"] In all editions 於 is corrupted as 與; it is now corrected on the authority of Beishi, juan 40, and Cefu yuangui, juan 472

sentences.zh: 〈五六二七頁〉
改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected.

sentences.zh: 亦可復舊 諸本「可」上有「不」字，北史卷四０、冊府卷四七二

translations.literal: [On the phrase] "亦可復舊": in all editions there is 不 above 可; Beishi, juan 40; Cefu yuangui, juan 472
translations.idiomatic: [Phrase "亦可復舊"] All editions have 不 above 可; Beishi, juan 40; Cefu yuangui, juan 472

sentences.zh: 〈五六二七頁〉
無。

translations.literal: do not have it.
translations.idiomatic: do not have it.

sentences.zh: 按若云「不可復舊」，則無需申說。

translations.literal: Comment: If it read "不可復舊", further explanation would be unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: If it read "不可復舊", further explanation would be unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 「不」字衍，今據刪。

translations.literal: The character 不 is superfluous; we now delete it on that evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The character 不 is superfluous and is now deleted on that evidence.

sentences.zh: 豈周急不繼富之謂也 諸本「急」訛「給」。

translations.literal: [On the phrase] "豈周急不繼富之謂也": in all editions 急 is corrupted as 給.
translations.idiomatic: [Phrase "豈周急不繼富之謂也"] In all editions 急 is corrupted as 給.

sentences.zh: 今據北史卷四０、冊府

translations.literal: Now corrected on the authority of Beishi, juan 40, and Cefu yuangui
translations.idiomatic: It is now corrected on the authority of Beishi, juan 40, and Cefu yuangui

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same juan and page〉

sentences.zh: 及論語雍也章原文改。

translations.literal: and the original text of the Yong ye chapter of the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: and the original text of the Yong ye chapter of the Analects.

sentences.zh: 敕御師徐謇診視 北史卷四０程駿傳「御師」上有「侍」字，與本書卷九一徐謇傳合，這裏當脫「侍」字。

translations.literal: [On the passage] "敕御師徐謇診視": In Beishi, juan 40, Cheng Jun biography, above 御師 there is the character 侍; this agrees with the Xu Qian biography in juan 91 of this book — here 侍 must have been omitted.
translations.idiomatic: [Passage "敕御師徐謇診視"] In Beishi, juan 40, Cheng Jun biography, the character 侍 appears before 御師; this agrees with the Xu Qian biography in juan 91 of this book — here 侍 must have been omitted.
